info.title: 0xinsider API
info.description: Follow provider-exposed large-trade activity on Polymarket sports and esports markets. The API serves sports and esports markets only: a market, event or trade outside them answers 404 not_found with error.reason=market_out_of_scope, which is terminal, so do not retry it, and a category outside them answers 400 bad_request with error.param=category, except on GET /api/v1/edge-hunter, where in every view a category that maps to no sport answers an empty result whose selection.category is non_sport. Polymarket wallet-attributed trades can add grades, P&L, strategy, and diagnostic-score context when sufficient source data exists. Fields can be null or unavailable. Normal API requests use a 30-second server timeout that returns HTTP 408 Request Timeout with the standard error envelope (error.code request_timeout) when exceeded. Every /api/v1 failure answers that envelope, including a body that is not JSON or does not fit the request schema (400 invalid_body), a query or path value that does not parse (400 invalid_query, invalid_path), a missing Content-Type: application/json (415 unsupported_media_type), a body over 1048576 bytes (413 payload_too_large) and a method the path does not serve (405 method_not_allowed), each with error.param naming the field where one is known and meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id. Unknown query names are ignored by default and reported in X-Query-Ignored, while X-Effective-Query lists the normalized names and values applied using form-urlencoded decoding, where + is a space; strict mode returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including for an unknown name with an incomplete percent escape. Every list operation clamps an out-of-range limit into its published minimum..maximum instead of refusing it (limit=0 reads one row, limit=500 reads the maximum), and X-Effective-Query reports the clamped value; only a limit that is not an integer is refused, with 400 invalid_query. Public REST /api/v1/* endpoints, excluding /api/v1/mcp, use Bearer-token based non-credentialed browser CORS: any Origin may call with Authorization, Content-Type, If-None-Match, Idempotency-Key, Mcp-Session-Id, Mcp-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Last-Event-Id, and X-Query-Validation request headers. X-Query-Validation: strict opts into rejecting unknown query names; the default remains compatible. Remote MCP at /api/v1/mcp is non-credentialed, but still validates Origin against the 0xinsider/localhost allowlist per MCP Streamable HTTP DNS-rebinding guidance. Successful browser CORS preflight responses advertise Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400. Browser JavaScript may read RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, X-Request-Cost, X-Usage-Accounting, X-Batch-RateLimit-Limit, X-Batch-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Batch-RateLimit-Reset, X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, X-Monthly-Quota-Reset, X-Query-Ignored, X-Effective-Query, Deprecation, Sunset, Link, and Server-Timing response headers. Rate-limit headers describe the budget a request was counted against: the API key's per-minute window, at its plan's limit, on an authenticated call, and the per-IP budget on a public route or on a refused credential (401, 402, 403, 423), so a client looping on a bad or lapsed key still sees how much room it has. Conditional GET: these operations return a weak ETag and answer If-None-Match with 304 Not Modified and an empty body: GET /api/v1/health, GET /api/v1/insider-radar, GET /api/v1/insider-radar/{id}, GET /api/v1/large-positions, GET /api/v1/leaderboard, GET /api/v1/leaderboard/trending, GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/candles, GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/flow, GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/intel, GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/snapshot, GET /api/v1/markets/explore, GET /api/v1/markets/sharp-money-flows, GET /api/v1/markets/smart-money-flows, GET /api/v1/pick-of-the-day, GET /api/v1/pick-of-the-day/archive, GET /api/v1/positions, GET /api/v1/trader/{address}, GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/context, GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/pnl, GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/position-timeline, GET /api/v1/traders/{trader}/position-timeline, GET /api/v1/large-trades, GET /api/v1/large-trades/history, GET /api/v1/large-trades/{id}, GET /api/v1/whale-trades, GET /api/v1/whale-trades/history, GET /api/v1/whale-trades/{id}, GET /api/v1/whale-trades/{id}/counterparties/executions, GET /api/v1/whale-trades/{id}/counterparties/executions/{execution_id}/makers. Credentialed first-party routes such as /api/keys, /api/billing, and auth endpoints remain restricted to configured 0xinsider origins. Protected V1 responses, except the zero-cost /api/v1/usage route, after handler execution carry X-Usage-Accounting: persisted, failed, or unknown. This reports the usage-record write; it does not change the handler result. Do not replay a successful mutation to repair an unknown usage record. Before execution, unavailable accounting capacity returns HTTP 503 with error.reason=request_accounting_unavailable; honor Retry-After. Public API responses add the browser-readable Server-Timing header: Processing time in milliseconds, for example api;dur=12.345. Includes API authentication, quota admission, handler work and response construction. Excludes network transit and streamed body or export-file transfer. The engineering budget is strictly below 250 ms; this header reports observations, not a latency guarantee or a new timeout. Requests through https://0xinsider.com/api/* append Server-Timing: web_api;dur=<milliseconds> and X-Web-Request-Id for that web origin handler. The web clock includes upstream waiting and existing body construction, so do not add it to api;dur. It excludes platform routing, cold module initialization, CDN hits and later stream/file transfer. On a cache hit these headers describe the earlier origin fill, not the current request; static Markdown API routes have no fresh web clock. GET /api/v1/edge-hunter supports conditional reads only with view=signals or view=observations; view=board does not emit ETag or return 304.

servers.description: Production (live data). Authenticate with a live key (oxi_sk_live_...); requires an active Pro subscription. A sandbox key (oxi_sk_test_...) is answered with 401 invalid_api_key and error.reason sandbox_api_key.

Sandbox. No credential required and no production data: every documented operation answers with its documented example or a deterministic sample of its response schema. GET /api/v1/stream is the one exclusion and answers 400 there, because a Server-Sent Events stream is a live connection rather than a body. Add ?sandbox_status=<code> to receive one of the error responses the operation documents (for example 429 with Retry-After). Documented query parameters and JSON request bodies are checked against this document, the two context.md routes answer 200 text/markdown, GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/export/download answers its 302 with a Location the sandbox serves itself rather than an object store, and nothing is stored between requests. A sandbox key (oxi_sk_test_..., issued with no account by POST https://api.0xinsider.com/api/v1/agents/register) is optional: on an operation that requires a credential, a well-formed key is answered with X-Oxi-Sandbox-Key: valid and a malformed one with 401 invalid_api_key.

get.description: Unauthenticated API-origin discovery document pointing agents to the canonical API base URL, full docs, web-origin OpenAPI spec, health check, and the COMPLETE index of authenticated data routes. data.authenticated_routes is the whole authenticated route surface, not a sample: it carries every authenticated route this spec documents, so an agent that starts here never has to guess a path. The index is a hand-maintained const in backend/src/api_v1/discovery.rs kept in step with this spec by review; no automated check compares the two, so treat this spec as authoritative if they ever disagree.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

data.authentication: Bearer API key required for data endpoints; discovery (/api/v1), health, coverage (/api/v1/coverage, and its deprecated alias /api/v1/platforms), the Pick of the Day commitment ledger (/api/v1/pick-of-the-day/ledger), and the MCP handshake (initialize, ping, tools/list on /api/v1/mcp) are public. A 401 carries WWW-Authenticate with the resource_metadata URL.

408.description: The handler did not answer inside the server's 30-second timeout. error.code is request_timeout. On GET and HEAD the response carries Retry-After and error.retry_at; on a mutation it carries neither, because the request may have completed on the server: check its state before repeating it, and reuse its Idempotency-Key.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

post.summary: Register an agent for a sandbox key
post.description: Self-serve agent onboarding: no account, no request body, no human step. Returns a sandbox API key (oxi_sk_test_...) and the path to live access. The key works only on the sandbox server (https://0xinsider.com/sandbox/api/v1), where it is optional: send it as Authorization: Bearer to exercise the credential path, and the sandbox answers a malformed key with the production 401. Nothing is stored, so the key cannot be listed or revoked and does not expire; register again for a new one. The live API answers a sandbox key with 401 invalid_api_key and error.reason sandbox_api_key. Live data needs an account with an active Pro subscription, and either an oxi_sk_live_ key from https://0xinsider.com/developers or an OAuth access token (https://0xinsider.com/auth.md). The request body is not read.

get.description: Returns a trader's grade (S through F), P&L, win rate, and optional strategy/category data. The path accepts either an Ethereum wallet address, a known trader username, or a trd_-prefixed trader ID emitted by this API. A wallet address this API does not track yet returns 200 with sync_status "unknown" instead of 404, so it can be polled. A value that is not a wallet address and matches no username or trader ID this API knows returns 404 not_found with error.param address; it is never echoed back as a trader address. The additive `stats.exact.total_volume` field carries a decimal string with unit, scale and basis metadata; parse it with decimal-safe arithmetic and keep the numeric twin for display. P&L and stats cover sports and esports markets only (#29830): `pnl.in_scope` (#27311) is the wallet's sports and esports record, the P&L the 0xinsider profile headlines, and `stats` counts the same markets. The wallet-wide `pnl.total`, `pnl.net_total`, `pnl.realized`, `pnl.exact`, `pnl.correction` and `stats.daily_win_rate` are deprecated and never sent since 2026-10-27; `pnl.unrealized` stays wallet-wide.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Ethereum wallet address (0x...), known trader username, or trd_-prefixed trader ID emitted by this API.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Include heavy fields and trust metadata. Repeatable: strategy, categories, trust. quant_metrics is accepted and returns nothing since 2026-10-27.

parameters.name: max_age_s
parameters.description: Opt into a whole-response freshness ceiling in seconds. The server returns 200 only when data_quality.status is fresh and data_quality.as_of is no older than this value; otherwise it returns 409 with error.reason=freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied. No refresh or alternate read is attempted.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Conditional GET validator from a previous ETag. Matching values return 304 Not Modified with an empty body.

total_volume.basis: trader_trade_daily_rollups.in_scope_volume_total (sum over every stored trade day; sports and esports markets)

strategy.description: Mixed activity across 1,802 stored markets. No single observed behavior has a clear lead. Category shares describe recorded USD cost basis; style is separate from performance.

field_groups.reason: only S, A and B wallets are given a leaderboard rank
open-position unrealized P&L is served, but no successful position snapshot or sync clock is available

409.description: The opt-in max_age_s ceiling could not be met. error.reason is freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied; error.freshness carries the requested ceiling, the measured age when available, the stored as_of clock, and data_quality_status. No refresh or alternate read is attempted.

304.description: Not Modified. Returned when If-None-Match matches the current payload.

402.description: Active Pro subscription required. The key is valid but the account has no active Pro subscription; error.reason is subscription_inactive and error.message names the reactivation URL (https://0xinsider.com/billing). Permanent until a person reactivates: no Retry-After, never retry on a schedule.

404.description: The address value names no trader: it is not a wallet address, and no username or trader ID this API knows matches it. error.code is not_found and error.param is address. A wallet address 0xinsider does not track yet is not an error; it returns 200 with sync_status "unknown".

get.description: Returns a single human- and LLM-readable Markdown briefing for one trader: identity, grade, P&L, position coverage, and freshness. The path accepts an Ethereum wallet address (0x...), a known trader username, or a trd_-prefixed trader ID emitted by this API. A wallet address this API does not track yet still returns 200 with a degraded 'not yet synced' document (no 404). A value that is not a wallet address and matches no username or trader ID this API knows returns 404 not_found with error.param address, as the JSON error envelope. The Markdown variant does not emit an ETag and does not support conditional requests; use the JSON variant (drop the .md suffix) for ETag/If-None-Match handling.

get.description: Returns one wallet's win record in every canonical category it has a settled market in: wins, decided (wins plus losses) and the rate, per category, busiest category first. These are the same counts the Pick of the Day holder chips carry. The Esports record also carries games: the wallet's record in each esports title it has a settled market in (LoL, CS2, Dota 2, Valorant, ...), the same per-game record the holder chips and GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/holders name in category_win_rate_game, with the same counts, floor and status rule; the Esports row itself stays the whole bucket, which is what a chip falls back to when a game record is thin. The basis is every settled market at any position size, which is NOT the basis of category_strengths on GET /api/v1/trader/{address}?expand=categories: that breakdown keeps the 20 USD notional floor and the entry-price rule its ranks depend on, so the two legitimately differ, in both directions. Measured on production 2026-09-22 over the 122,497 wallet-category pairs with at least 20 decided markets on both bases: the floored rate was higher in 56.5% of pairs, lower in 34.5% and equal in 9.0%, median +0.6 points, p10 -4.6, p90 +9.8, and 14.0% of pairs differ by 10 points or more. Neither rate corrects the other. The difference is not only small positions: on a 1-in-250 wallet sample the same day, admitted markets won 56.6% while markets dropped by the notional floor alone won 45.2% and markets dropped by the entry-price rule alone won 48.7%. The two tables also run on different clocks, this one rebuilt daily and that breakdown updated incrementally, so a same-day read can differ on timing alone. A category or game with fewer than min_decided_for_win_rate decided markets keeps its counts and returns win_rate null with status not_enough_data, so a caller can apply its own sample rule. A category the wallet has no settled market in is omitted entirely, and so is a game: an absent entry means no record, never a 0% record. A resolved trader with no settled market returns an empty records array (HTTP 200); an unknown address returns 404. Sports and esports only (#27311): records cover sports and esports categories only, so a wallet whose settled markets are all elsewhere returns an empty records array.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

get.description: Returns a trader's sports and esports daily P&L time series and pre-derived stats: entries (daily realized P&L and its running sum), period stats (all/90d/30d/7d), monthly aggregation, per-year totals, the drawdown series, series_status, and realized, which reconciles the days with the wallet's Sports P&L (pnl.in_scope.realized_pnl on GET /api/v1/trader/{address}): the days plus realized.undated_pnl equal it. A day's daily_change is the realized P&L of the wallet's sports and esports markets dated to that UTC day, the resolution day for a settled market, else the last trade day. series_status pending means the series is not computed yet; its empty sections never mean zero. A resolved trader with no sports or esports day returns an empty structured object (HTTP 200), as does a wallet that traded no sports or esports market (series_status ready, realized null, freshness_at its last completed sync; since 2026-10-29, #30589, #30657) or that trades only combos and holds no single sports or esports market (the same; since 2026-10-29, #30637); an unknown address returns 404. Optional from/to and sections bound what comes back: from/to clip the two daily series (entries, drawdown) to an inclusive UTC date window, and sections names which of the five sections the body carries. A request that sends none of the three receives the whole object and no data.view. A body built with any of them carries data.view, which names the bounds, the sections applied, the size of the full series and the last daily point before the window; a section the request excluded is absent from data, not null or empty. stats, monthly and year_totals keep their full-period definitions whatever the window says, so an economic value never changes meaning because a chart asked for seven days.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Wallet address (0x...), username, or trd_-prefixed trader id.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive UTC calendar-date lower bound in YYYY-MM-DD form for the daily series (entries and drawdown). Omit for the whole stored history. A value that is not a calendar date, or a from later than to, returns 400 bad_request with error.param from. Does not change stats, monthly or year_totals, which stay defined over the full history.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive UTC calendar-date upper bound in YYYY-MM-DD form for the daily series (entries and drawdown). Omit for the whole stored history. A value that is not a calendar date returns 400 bad_request with error.param to. Does not change stats, monthly or year_totals.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Which sections of the object to return. Repeatable and comma-separated: entries, stats, monthly, year_totals, drawdown. Omit it, or send it empty, for all five. A section left out is absent from data. An unrecognized name returns 400 bad_request with error.param sections rather than being ignored, so a typo cannot look like a successful request that silently dropped the section you came for.

get.description: Unified trader-timeline route (#4975). {trader} accepts all five identity shapes - 0x... wallet, username, trd_-prefixed trader id, bare integer id, and @username (a username lookup only, for all-digit usernames) - resolved by the single shared trader-identity resolver. Returns stored Polymarket fills for one tracked trader in one market, newest first, with server-computed running_amount and running_avg_price. Stored fills start 2026-07-17; the timeline returns no fill before that date. Only warm-tier traders, the wallets we sync most often, are tracked; other traders return 404. Response payload matches the singular GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/position-timeline route for the same (trader, market), except for the per-request meta.request_id. The prior integer-id-only variant is preserved: the same path now accepts every identity shape.

Permanent until a person reactivates: no Retry-After, never retry on a schedule.

404.description: Not found. On this route a 404 has THREE distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="trader_not_tracked": the wallet is real and the URL is right, but the trader is not on the warm sync tier (the wallets we sync most often), so we capture no timeline for them. This is TERMINAL -- there is no Retry-After and no error.retry_at, because neither retrying nor re-spelling the path will ever succeed. Stop requesting this wallet. (2) no error.reason: the trader id or address does not resolve at all. Both carry error.code="not_found" (a FROZEN contract value), so error.reason is the discriminator -- and since this endpoint has singular and plural path spellings, "I used the wrong URL" is a plausible enough wrong guess that the distinction is worth branching on. (3) error.reason="market_out_of_scope" (#27311): condition_id names a market outside sports and esports, which 0xinsider serves exclusively. This is terminal too: stop requesting this market.

get.x-snapshot-consistency: With consistency=snapshot and at least one wallet, the server freezes at most 500 matching rows and 2 MB of position data for up to five minutes. One snapshot per API key is retained; a new first-page snapshot replaces the prior one. A missing, replaced, or expired snapshot returns cursor_expired and the client starts at page one. Snapshot consistency does not imply complete provider coverage.
get.description: Returns the current positions-board feed backed by the wallet_positions mirror. Ordered by current_value_usd DESC with deterministic (wallet, condition_id, outcome_index) tiebreakers. Pre-reconcile rows (current_value_usd IS NULL) are excluded. Positions on resolved markets are excluded: a position leaves the feed when its market resolves, so a condition_id read of a resolved market returns no rows. Positions on markets outside sports and esports are excluded on every read, the board and wallet reads included. Cursor-paginated. Every filter pushes into SQL. Deep cursor pages cost the same as the first page: the value bounds and the cursor are index conditions, so a page never rescans the feed from the top. With wallet, the same feed is read for one wallet or a book of up to 25 wallets from each wallet's own ordered index range, so the pages are that wallet's complete reconciled binary open positions on sports and esports markets and the cost is the page, never the board. min_size defaults to 100 on the board read, so a request with no wallet and no min_size drops positions valued under 100 USD; with wallet it defaults to 0 instead. Send min_size=0 to include every reconciled position. What a wallet read does not return: positions with shares at 0 (closed), positions on resolved markets (redeemable or already redeemed), positions on markets outside sports and esports, rows the reconciler has not valued yet (current_value_usd IS NULL), and non-binary outcomes; per-row last_reconciled_at and freshness say how old each valuation is. Each row also carries additive `exact` source atoms as decimal strings with unit, scale and basis metadata; parse those values with decimal-safe arithmetic and do not reconstruct them from the display-safe numeric fields. The response adds a top-level `data_quality` object beside `data`, with positions, trader, and market groups owned by `wallet_positions.last_reconciled_at|updated_at`, `traders.last_synced`, and `market_canonical.last_refreshed_at`. Its stored clocks are part of the ETag; `meta` continues to hold transport cache facts.

parameters.description: Maximum number of current positions to return. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from previous response's next_cursor.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: live (default) reads the current value-ordered board. snapshot requires wallet and freezes up to 500 matching rows and 2 MB for up to five minutes. Keep consistency=snapshot and the same effective filters on every page; changing filters returns 400. A new first page from the same API key replaces its prior snapshot; replacement or expiry returns cursor_expired.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: Minimum current position value in USD. Defaults to 100 when omitted, or to 0 when wallet is present; send 0 to include every reconciled position.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Exact match against provider-backed market_canonical.category. Sports and esports only (#27311): a category outside them returns 400 bad_request with param category and names the accepted buckets.

parameters.name: condition_id
parameters.description: Scope to one market. Accepts the raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id emitted by V1 responses. Combine with min_size=0 for every reconciled position in that market; an unknown id or a resolved market returns []. A market outside sports and esports returns 404 not_found with error.reason=market_out_of_scope (#27311). Without condition_id the board and wallet reads list sports and esports markets only.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Scope to one wallet or a book of wallets (repeatable, up to 25 per request; comma-separated values inside one occurrence also work). Each value is a wallet address, a known username, or a trd_-prefixed trader id, resolved like /api/v1/trader/{address}. The response keeps the board's order and cursor, so pages of a book interleave wallets by current_value_usd. An address this API has never tracked returns its mirror rows or an empty list; a username or trader id that resolves to nothing is a 404 naming wallet; more than 25 values is a 400. min_size defaults to 0 when wallet is present.

parameters.name: min_grade
parameters.description: Minimum trader grade allowlist. `A` matches S and A; `B` matches S, A, B; etc.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Filter by the binary outcome side. `yes` maps to outcome_index=0, `no` to outcome_index=1.

get.description: Returns the largest current open positions from graded traders, value-descending, with opaque cursor pagination. This is a change-detection feed, not a holder list: a row needs a current value of at least 50,000 USD and a live detection in the last 24 hours, so a wallet that holds a market without moving is not listed. For every graded holder of one market use GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/holders. Polymarket-only by design: the large-positions scanner filters platform = 'polymarket' (backend/crates/large-positions/src/scanner.rs), so only Polymarket rows are scanned and an unknown condition_id filter returns an empty list (never fabricated rows). Sports and esports markets only (#27305): a position on a market outside product scope is not listed; a condition_id naming one returns 404 not_found with error.reason=market_out_of_scope, and a category outside sports and esports returns 400 bad_request with param=category. The teaser cap that the internal product UI applies to anonymous viewers does not apply here: the API key already proves an active Pro subscription (wire tier `insider`), so authed API callers get full access.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

parameters.description: Maximum number of large positions to return. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: Minimum position value in USD. Raises the feed's own floor of 50,000 USD; a smaller value does not lower it.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: One RFC 4180 CSV record of exact current provider-backed market_canonical.category values. get.description: Returns historical large trades from local whale_alerts rows, not request-time provider fetches. Filter by condition_id, trader, category, minimum grade, persisted suspicion, platform, and RFC3339 from/to windows. All filters are pushed into SQL before LIMIT, every request uses SQL-backed limit + 1 pagination, and results are ordered newest first by traded_at desc, id desc. Metadata exposes local_replay source and best_effort completeness. Returns trades on sports and esports markets only (#27430), across the whole archive: a stored trade on any other market is left out before LIMIT. POINT IN TIME: signal_score, trader.grade and the min_grade filter carry today's values on every row however old, so a backtest that selects by them selects wallets on what they did after the trade. The point-in-time fields are recorded_signal_score (from 2026-08-03T11:59Z; null before, and never backfilled, because the trader statistics it reads at insert were not kept for older rows) and trader.grade_at_trade with trader.grade_at_trade_status (from 2026-09-19T23:00Z; unknown before). CAPTURE RULES changed over the archive's life: rows before 2026-02-02 are sparse (at most a few hundred a month); from 2026-02-02 the floor was 3,000 USD (1.4% of rows through 2026-07-05 are smaller) and trades at any price were kept; from 2026-07-06 a trade is kept at 10,000 USD or more (1,000 USD in earnings markets) and only when priced below 0.97 (0.99 in earnings markets). Pass min_size=10000 for one size rule across the whole range; monthly row counts still follow the sports calendar. Until 2026-07-17 one match could be stored twice, once per wallet: from 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-17, 27.7% of rows at 10,000 USD or more share a transaction and market with another stored wallet, almost always a Yes buyer and a No buyer filled against each other. From 2026-07-18 a row is the taker's side only. Before 2026-05 the transaction hash is mostly absent, so the share cannot be measured there. From 2026-09-23 a fill must ALSO be at least 0.1% of its market's recorded traded volume, Polymarket's own share count, so a $10,000 print that lands in a market which has already traded tens of millions of shares is no longer kept; rows written before that date were not re-filtered. 429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. get.description: Returns historical whale trades from local whale_alerts rows, not request-time provider fetches. Filter by condition_id, trader, category, minimum grade, persisted suspicion, platform, and RFC3339 from/to windows. All filters are pushed into SQL before LIMIT, every request uses SQL-backed limit + 1 pagination, and results are ordered newest first by traded_at desc, id desc. Metadata exposes local_replay source and best_effort completeness. Returns trades on sports and esports markets only (#27430), across the whole archive: a stored trade on any other market is left out before LIMIT. Deprecated alias of GET /api/v1/large-trades/history, kept live until its sunset on 2027-02-01 (#16304, #29351); every response carries `Deprecation: @1790132400` (RFC 9745, 2026-09-23T03:00:00Z) and a `Link` to the successor (`rel="successor-version"`) and to the versioning policy (`rel="deprecation"`). `Sunset: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT` (RFC 8594) names that date, after which the path answers 410 Gone with error.code endpoint_retired. The response adds a top-level `data_quality` object beside `data`, grouping alert, trade, trader, ranking, market, and volume fields by their database writer. `whale_alerts.inserted_xid` is reported as unknown because it is a transaction identifier rather than a timestamp. Its stored clocks are part of the ETag; `meta` continues to hold transport cache facts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of historical large trades to return. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from previous response's next_cursor. Prefix: wth_. URL-encode when replaying as a query parameter.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: Minimum trade size in USD.

parameters.name: condition_id
parameters.description: Exact raw provider condition_id. Unknown markets return an empty list.

parameters.name: trader
parameters.description: Trader wallet address, timestamp-suffixed wallet alias, or username resolved against the traders table. Unknown traders return an empty list.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by market category (case-insensitive). A canonical bucket name (e.g. Basketball) matches every provider member that folds into it (NBA, WNBA, NCAAB); a raw provider value also resolves to its bucket. Sports and esports only (#27430): a category outside them returns 400 bad_request with param category and names the accepted buckets.

parameters.name: min_grade
parameters.description: Minimum trader grade.

parameters.name: suspicious_only
parameters.description: When true, return only rows with persisted suspicion_score >= 60. The filter is applied before SQL-backed limit + 1 pagination.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Filter by whale_alerts.platform. all is equivalent to omitted.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 lower bound on whale_alerts.traded_at.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive RFC3339 upper bound on whale_alerts.traded_at. Must be after from when both are present.

parameters.name: min_market_volume_share
parameters.description: Keep only trades whose market_volume_share is known and at least this. A fraction, not a percent: 0.01 is one percent of the market's traded volume. A trade whose share is unavailable is never returned by a non-zero value, because an unavailable share cannot be said to clear a floor.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order of the returned page. recent is newest first and is the default. market_volume_share ranks by each trade's share of its market's traded volume, biggest first, with a trade whose share is unavailable last. That ranking reads from, or the last 30 days when from is omitted, for the same reason. A cursor is bound to the order it was minted in, so a continuation cannot cross from one order into the other.

parameters.name: event_slug
parameters.description: Only the large trades in one game: every market of the game behind this event slug, the moneyline, spreads, totals and props, as GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug}/trades reads them. Matched case-insensitively. Newest first only (sort=market_volume_share answers 400), and cannot be combined with condition_id (400). An unknown slug answers 404 not_found with error.param event_slug.

get.description: Returns ranked traders (grades S/A/B), by default in the board's own order: score descending, with a fixed tiebreak so the order never changes between reads of one ranking generation. sort, dir and activity reorder and scope the same wallets the way the site's leaderboard does (since 2026-11-02, #32237). Supports cursor pagination and optional category/strategy filters. A sorted or activity-scoped page reads the serving projection only; while that projection is older than its 300 s freshness bound it answers 503 rate_limit_unavailable with error.reason read_model_warming and Retry-After, and the default order keeps serving.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of ranked traders to return. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque lbv1_ pagination cursor from a prior response. It binds the finite score/address boundary to the committed leaderboard generation and the effective category/strategy filters, and on a sorted page to its sort, dir and activity. A cursor from another sort or dir is a 400 bad_request on cursor; one from another activity, category, strategy or generation is cursor_expired. Legacy, malformed, non-finite, and unsupported-version cursors are rejected.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by category: a sport or esports bucket. Values are matched to canonical category buckets: league values fold into their sport (NBA and NCAAB into Basketball, NFL into Football). Mapped buckets are case-insensitive; passthrough buckets (Cricket, Sports) match case-sensitively against the provider-native bucket key, so use exact casing. Sports and esports only (#27306): a category outside them returns 400 bad_request with param category and names the accepted buckets.

parameters.name: strategy
parameters.description: Filter by observed trading style. Current styles: two_sided, category_focused, high_activity, diversified, mixed, unclassified. Current styles count the wallet's sports and esports markets only. The ten archetype keys retired on 2026-10-01 (accumulator, algo_trader, arbitrageur, directional, event_driven, market_maker, momentum, scalper, speculator, swing_trader) are still accepted and match no wallet. Style describes recorded behavior; grade measures performance.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order of the list, the sort columns of the site's leaderboard (/skill-leaderboard). rank (default) is the board's own order, the rank the site and the trader profile show. grade orders by score. volume orders by sports and esports USD volume, the figure GET /api/v1/trader/{address} serves as stats.total_volume. predictions orders by markets_traded. pnl orders by in_scope.realized_pnl. win_rate orders by win_rate among wallets with at least 5 decided sports and esports markets; a wallet with fewer sorts as having none. edge orders by price_edge.edge among wallets whose price_edge.status is ranked and that carry no price_edge.hold; any other wallet sorts as having none. The site's Edge column ranks those same wallets by their edge pulled toward the sports and esports average, a figure the API does not send, so the two orders can differ. A wallet without the value sorts as the lowest, so last in the natural direction and first with the direction reversed. Ties fall to address ascending. With ?category= a sort still orders by these whole-record figures; the category only decides which wallets are listed. Since 2026-11-02 (#32237; edge, #32270).

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Direction of sort. Omitted, each sort reads in its natural direction: rank 1 first for rank (asc), largest first for every other sort (desc). The opposite value reverses the list. Since 2026-11-02 (#32237).

parameters.name: activity
parameters.description: Limit the list to wallets by recent trading, the site leaderboard's split. active: the wallet's last trade, as its current grade recorded it and aged to today, is 30 days old or less. inactive: older than 30 days, or no trade on record. all (default): every ranked wallet. Since 2026-11-02 (#32237).

get.summary: Get today's or a past day's Pick of the Day
get.description:
Returns entitled published picks for the current product day, or for the past product day named by `date`. Pro includes five selections in total: the designated free selection and the first four non-free selections in publication order. Max opens every available selection, up to twenty-five. A day can include multiple selections from the same game. Same-game picks share exposure and need not be independent; retain each `pick_id` instead of deduplicating by game. Both read resolved picks. Publication prices and backing are frozen. Without `date`, a prior day never appears here.

With `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, America/New_York, before today), the response is that day's slate as the dated web page shows it, under the same tier rule: resolved picks are open to both tiers, and unresolved picks outside the tier appear as `locked_picks`. A past day carries no `scheduled_picks`. A past day with no published pick returns a final 404 `not_found` with `error.param=date` and no retry guidance. Today's date is the same read as no `date`; a date after today returns 400 `bad_request` with `error.param=date`. The archive lists every published pick with its `pick_date`.

Stable `pick_id` values identify selections. `publication_order` describes presentation and `is_free_selection` describes access; neither is a quality rating. Standing selections retain their identity, slot, and release schedule. Later additions fill available slots. Historical IDs, order, and proof bytes remain unchanged.

Unauthorized unresolved selections appear only as identity-free `locked_picks` containing `pick_rank` and `required_tier`. When only locked selections are published, HTTP 200 carries `state=none`, `picks=[]`, `pick_count=0`, and an Upgrade to Max message. Proof warming applies only to entitled picks.

`scheduled_picks` contains only entitled slots and retains required `release_at` and `kickoff`. Unauthorized scheduled selections expose no game identity or release time.

For today, when no active pick is available, including after cancelled recommendations are withdrawn, HTTP 404 carries `error.code="not_found"` and `error.reason="pick_not_released"`. Branch on the reason and schedule one request using `Retry-After` or `error.retry_at` instead of polling. This advisory retry does not reveal an unauthorized game's release time.

Final sporting scores are retained for resolved picks after the event is confirmed ended and both sides have verified scores. A result without a verified final stays unavailable; a win/loss outcome alone does not establish a sporting score. Existing sports_context fields and return calculations are unchanged.

Withdrawn picks are excluded from current and dated recommendations, the archive, and its statistics, even after market settlement. The public ledger retains every published commitment under its original identity and proof bytes. Provider settlement still determines the recorded result. Request and response fields are unchanged.

get.summary: Get the Pick of the Day commitment ledger
get.description:
Returns the pre-game commitment for every published pick, so the public track record can be checked by someone who was not watching when the pick dropped.

One entry per (pick_date, pick_rank), ascending by pick_date then pick_rank, in one of three states. `sealed` is an unresolved pick: the hash, the algorithm, the seal instant, and nothing that states a side or a price. `opened` is a settled pick: the nonce and the exact canonical payload the hash was taken over. `uncommitted` is a pick with no commitment -- published before the scheme existed, or one that reached kickoff unsealed -- named rather than omitted.

To verify an opened entry: serialize nothing. Take the bytes of the `payload` object exactly as received, append the `commitment_nonce` decoded from hex, and sha256 the result; it equals `commitment_hash`. The payload is canonical JSON -- keys sorted by UTF-8 byte value, no insignificant whitespace, decimals as strings at full stored precision, timestamps whole-second UTC with a literal Z -- and it is served byte for byte as it was hashed.

This is a proof contract, not the archive's display contract: nothing here is formatted for rendering, so an entry changes only when the pick does. Unresolved ledger entries omit game identity and kickoff; sealed_at remains public commitment provenance. A commitment is never written after kickoff and never rewritten by an outcome correction; `resolved_at` moving under an unchanged `commitment_hash` is a corrected market re-mapping an already-settled pick.

Withdrawal from current recommendations or the product archive does not remove a published ledger entry. The ledger retains every published commitment under its original identity and proof bytes; canonical market settlement still determines the recorded result.

get.description: Returns wallets ranked by Polymarket weekly/monthly P&L (Polymarket-only discovery), with opaque page-cursor pagination. trending_pnl_usd and the by-PNL row order come from Polymarket's canonical leaderboard (data-api.polymarket.com/v2/leaderboard?time_period=week|month&sort_by=PNL), not a locally summed realized-leaf total. Each row also carries window volume, distinct markets, grade, hot-streak tier, and daily_pnl_series: the wallet's sports and esports realized P&L on each UTC day of the window, with daily_pnl_series_status ready or pending (pending: the series is empty and never means zero). It leaves out non-sports markets, so it does not sum to trending_pnl_usd. The response comes from a retained Redis board: meta.cached is true, and meta.cache_age_s reports the original board age when known (omitted when unknown). A backend read of a board at least 120 seconds old attempts a detached refresh; after a quiet spell a product board may be up to a day old. HTTP freshness ends at 120 seconds; max-age plus stale-while-revalidate cannot exceed the remaining original retention. Unknown age grants no cache window. A true cold read returns 503 (warming, retry-after), never a fabricated ranking. Polymarket-only: the read model filters platform = 'polymarket'. Cursors are bound to the effective limit, window and ranked-board generation; a changed board or request scope returns 400 with error.reason=cursor_expired, and legacy page-only cursors must restart from page one.

The key is valid but the account has no active Pro subscription; error.reason is subscription_inactive and error.message names the reactivation URL (https://0xinsider.com/billing). Permanent until a person reactivates: no Retry-After, never retry on a schedule.

408.description: The handler did not answer inside the server's 30-second timeout. error.code is request_timeout. On GET and HEAD the response carries Retry-After and error.retry_at; on a mutation it carries neither, because the request may have completed on the server: check its state before repeating it, and reuse its Idempotency-Key.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

503.description: Service unavailable. On this route a 503 has TWO distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="read_model_warming": the requested endpoint cannot serve its read model yet. Exact causes are endpoint-specific and can include a cold or contended refresh or a dependency that prevented refresh; consult that endpoint's contract and do not infer dependency health from this shared reason. This is endpoint-local unavailability, not rate limiting: retry only this route after Retry-After (or error.retry_at), and do not feed it into a rate-limit backoff shared with other endpoints. (2) no error.reason: the Redis-backed authenticated rate limiter is unavailable and the middleware failed closed; Retry-After is the seconds until it probes Redis again. Both carry error.code="rate_limit_unavailable" (a FROZEN contract value, so it cannot be split per cause) and X-Request-Id -- which is why error.reason, not error.code, is the discriminator.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until retrying is worth doing. With error.reason="read_model_warming" this is the endpoint-local read-model retry interval; without a reason it is the rate-limiter outage cooldown. Always >= 1.

get.summary: Get a sport or league leaderboard
get.description: One sport's skill leaderboard, or with `league` one league's, the board the site's sport pages show. Wallets need `min_resolved` resolved markets in the sport or league. `sort=edge` (the default) ranks `edge_skill`, the edge over the price paid pulled toward the board's `edge_average` by how much of the record is noise; a wallet without a ranked edge sorts after the ranked ones. `sort=pnl` ranks realized P&L, and `sort=win_rate` the Wilson lower bound of the win rate. Boards are ranked to 100 wallets; `limit` returns the head of that list. A sport slug outside sports and esports is 404 with error.param=sport; a league slug the sport has no board for is 404 with error.param=league (GET /api/v1/leaderboard/leagues lists them). 503 read_model_warming while the ranking is being rebuilt.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description: A league slug of the sport, for example premier-league or cs2, from GET /api/v1/leaderboard/leagues. Omit it for the sport board.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Ranking axis. Any other value returns 400 bad_request with error.param=sort.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows to return from the top of the board. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

get.summary: List every category's top edge leaders
get.description: Every sports and esports category's top three edge leaders in one read, the board the site's categories index shows. In each category, wallets are ranked as GET /api/v1/leaderboard/categories/{slug} ranks them, by the 95% lower bound of their edge over the price they paid; only wallets whose lower bound is above zero are listed, so a category can carry fewer than three, or none. Rows come by category, then rank, in the same row shape as the per-category board. Not paginated. 503 read_model_warming, with Retry-After, while the category-skill ranking is being rebuilt or its model is degraded: never an empty 200.

get.description: One sports or esports category's edge leaderboard, the board the site's category pages show. Wallets are ranked by edge_lower_bound, the 95% lower bound of their edge over the price they paid in the category, counted over independent events (independent_events breaks ties, then the wallet). Only wallets whose lower bound is above zero are listed; total counts them across every page. active_within keeps wallets that traded in the category within 7d, 30d or 90d, and min_events sets the independent events a wallet needs. A sibling of GET /api/v1/leaderboard and GET /api/v1/leaderboard/sports/{sport}, which rank the grade score and the settled-record edge; this ranking is the category-skill model's lower bound, with its own cursor. A slug outside sports and esports is 404 with error.param=slug. 503 read_model_warming, with Retry-After, while the category-skill ranking is being rebuilt or its model is degraded: never an empty 200.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The category slug, for example soccer, basketball, tennis or esports, as GET /api/v1/leaderboard/categories lists it lowercased. Matched case-insensitively.

parameters.name: active_within
parameters.description: Keep wallets that traded in the category within this window. all (the default) keeps every ranked wallet.

parameters.name: min_events
parameters.description: Independent events a wallet needs in the category to be listed. The site offers 0, 50, 100 and 250. Clamped to 0..1000000.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of leaders to return. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cel_ pagination cursor from a prior response. It binds the lower-bound/independent-event/wallet boundary to the committed category-skill ranking and to the slug, active_within and min_events of the request that issued it; a cursor from another filter is 400 on cursor, and one issued before the ranking refreshed is 400 with error.reason=cursor_expired.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Conditional GET validator from a previous ETag. Matching values return 304 Not Modified with an empty body.

200.description: One category's edge leaders, best lower bound first

ETag.description: Stable validator for the current page. Re-send it via If-None-Match for conditional GETs.

total.description: Wallets in the category whose edge lower bound is above zero, Wallets in the full walk across every page: those in the category, under this request's active_within and min_events, whose edge lower bound is above zero. The same on every page.

304.description: Not Modified. Returned when If-None-Match matches the current page of the category's ranking.

ETag.description: Validator for the unchanged leaderboard payload.

400.description: Bad request: active_within outside all, 7d, 30d, 90d (error.param=active_within), or a malformed cursor or one from another filter (error.param=cursor). error.reason=cursor_expired with error.param=cursor means the category-skill ranking refreshed since the cursor was issued: discard accumulated rows, request the first page again, and continue with its next_cursor. There is no retry delay.

On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

(2) no error.reason: the Redis-backed authenticated rate limiter is unavailable and the middleware failed closed; Retry-After is the seconds until it probes Redis again. Retry-After.description: Seconds until retrying is worth doing. With error.reason="read_model_warming" this is the endpoint-local read-model retry interval; without a reason it is the rate-limiter outage cooldown. Always >= 1.

get.summary: Which reads the API serves for Polymarket
get.description: Unauthenticated discovery endpoint that declares which V1 data surfaces the API serves for Polymarket, the one venue it covers. Every capability reports supported. Coverage is sports and esports markets only (#27299): a market outside them answers 404 not_found with error.reason market_out_of_scope, and a category filter outside them answers 400 bad_request with param category on the reads that filter by it: large trades and their history, large positions, the leaderboard, market search and explore, and sharp-money flows. GET /api/v1/positions and GET /api/v1/trader/{address}/categories do not refuse a category value (#27581). Canonical since #16315; GET /api/v1/platforms is its deprecated alias with the same body.

get.description: The graded holder roster of one market, the list a Pick of the Day shows for its market, for any Polymarket market: every S/A/B wallet with open shares on either outcome, from a complete provider holder scan, each with its shares, Polymarket's own currentValue for the leg, its grade, its win record in the market's category, and its badges. Both outcomes are listed; a wallet holding both is listed once on its net side. Ordered by current_value_usd DESC, then shares DESC, then address. The roster is computed at most once a minute per market and shared by every caller; a page is cut from that roster, so paging is cheap and `total` is exact. An answer whose scan saw no wallet at all (`scan.wallet_count` 0), on an open market before its end date, is kept for up to an hour while no trade in that market is seen after the scan; `meta.cache_age_s` gives its age. The route never widens past the graded cohort: `scan.wallet_count` reports every wallet the walk saw, graded or not. An incomplete, unstable or failed scan is a 503 with Retry-After, never a shorter list. Cold reads are shared per account (#28752): a request for a market with no cached roster and no cached complete scan walks Polymarket, and an account may start 6 such walks a minute, in bursts of up to 400. Over that share the answer is 429 rate_limited with error.reason cold_read_limited and Retry-After, and nothing is walked; a market whose roster or scan is cached, including one another caller just read, still answers and spends no share. A complete scan in which no S, A or B wallet holds either outcome is a 200 with an empty holders list and zero totals; retrying cannot change it. The cohort is S, A and B by the wallet's current grade (`traders.latest_grade`); a C, D, F or ungraded wallet is never listed here and appears only inside `scan.wallet_count`. A count here will not match GET /api/v1/positions for the same market, and the cohort is only one of three reasons: /positions reads the `wallet_positions` mirror rather than this live provider scan, and without a `wallet` its `min_size` defaults to 100 USD, so it drops the smaller legs this route keeps. Read a difference as all three, never as a grade count. This is current state and takes no as-of parameter: the roster is at most 60 s old over a provider walk at most 180 s old (an answer with no wallet at all, at most an hour), and `scan.fetched_at` is the only timestamp on it. For a point-in-time roster, snapshot this route yourself on your own schedule; the one frozen roster the API serves is `display_holders` on GET /api/v1/pick-of-the-day, for that pick's market and backed side at publication.

get.description: The largest holders of one market on each outcome, every grade from S to F and ungraded wallets included: the table the market's event page shows under Top holders. Each outcome lists up to 100 wallets, largest `shares` first, from Polymarket's holder board, with the provider's current value, average entry price and position P&L for the leg, the wallet's grade, its sports and esports realized P&L and volume, its win record in the market's category, and its badges. 429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

get.description: Provider-first bucketed OHLC price candles for a market's outcome tokens, derived from our stored copy of the Polymarket CLOB prices-history series (the same series the market-detail chart renders; covers open and resolved markets). Because the stored data is daily, a 1d bucket typically carries one point so its open/high/low/close all equal that day's close; 1w aggregates real OHLC across the observed daily closes. No intraday fidelity is fabricated. Query field names and recognized values are URL-decoded; duplicate recognized fields use the last value and unknown fields are ignored. When both bounds are present, from must be less than or equal to to; malformed or inverted bounds answer 400.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Bucketing granularity. 1d aggregates by UTC calendar day, 1w by ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC start). Defaults to 1d.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Exclusive lower bound as a URL-decoded unix timestamp in seconds; points at or before this timestamp are omitted (the underlying daily snapshot read filters bucket_start > from). If to is also present, from must be less than or equal to to. Note: for resolution=1w a surviving mid-week point can yield a weekly candle whose t (Monday 00:00 UTC) precedes from.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound as a URL-decoded unix timestamp in seconds; points after this timestamp are omitted. If from is also present, from must be less than or equal to to.

get.summary: Get a market's net buyers and sellers
get.description: One market's net buyers and net sellers over the last 24 hours or 7 days, live: the body the 0xinsider market page's wallets in/out panel reads for a Pro viewer, from the same aggregate and cache (reads are cached for up to 60 seconds). A wallet's net is its buys minus its sells in the window across both outcomes, in USD of matched notional, fees excluded. summary counts every wallet that traded the market in the window; net_buyers and net_sellers list the top 25 on each side. A wallet that bought and sold the same amount nets zero and is on neither list.

get.description: Stored trades whose recorded suspicion score meets the live flag threshold. Evidence contains the scorer's stored signals. Cursor-paginated by suspicion score. mode=live (default) uses fresh cached pages; mode=stable pins pagination to one published scoring generation and returns cursor_expired when scores or filters change. Sports and esports markets only (#27305): a flag on a market outside product scope is not listed, and the detail route answers it 404 not_found with error.reason=market_out_of_scope. Canonical since 2026-09-23; GET /api/v1/insider-radar is its deprecated alias.

get.description: One coherent game view per row: both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, and the game's winner markets (the moneyline, or a soccer game's three 1X2 legs) with their condition ids and outcome token ids. Built from the same provider-first live and upcoming projections the site's sports boards use, so a request pays no provider fan-out of its own. A finished status (ended, cancelled, postponed) also lists the games the board has dropped, from their stored records (freshness.source stored, as GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug} serves them), for kickoffs from starts_after (default 7 days before starts_before) to starts_before (default and cap: now); such a page can hold fewer than limit games, or none, while has_more is true, so follow next_cursor until has_more is false. Ordered by kickoff, then by event_slug; games whose kickoff the provider has not published sort last. For what is on now, pass window=now: without it the list starts at the oldest game still open, which can be weeks old. coverage names the sports and leagues this deployment serves and any scope whose source was unavailable for the read, so an empty page is never ambiguous. A sport or status outside the published vocabulary returns an empty page rather than a 400. Carries the board's existing competitor-bound provider moneyline price state by default, with an observation clock and explicit incomplete or invalid state. Each game also carries its traded volume (volume: value, unit, basis, source, observed_at) and each market its provider liquidity, so games can be ranked by activity without a Gamma call; a figure the board does not hold is omitted, never 0. It does not fetch another provider endpoint. Soccer 1X2 moneylines retain independent YES legs classified as home, draw and away; draw_offered is true when a classified draw leg is included. The event-level sharp-money split is opt-in through expand=sharp_money (Pro and Max); holder identities remain on their own gated routes.

parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. parameters.description: Canonical sport bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space: table-tennis and Table Tennis are the same bucket. Omit for every covered sport. A bucket this deployment does not serve returns an empty page.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description: League tag, case-insensitive, as coverage.leagues spells it: nfl, epl, cs2, euroleague, cbb, cwbb. EuroLeague games use sport=Basketball and league=euroleague; NCAA men's and women's college basketball games use sport=Basketball with league=cbb and league=cwbb. parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keep only games in this state. ended, cancelled and postponed also list finished games that have left the live board, read from their stored records, for kickoffs within starts_after..starts_before (default: the 7 days before now). parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description: RFC 3339 instant. Keep only games whose kickoff is at or after it. Games with no published kickoff are excluded whenever either bound is set.
