parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: RFC 3339 instant. Keep only games whose kickoff is at or before it. Must be at or after starts_after.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Which games to read. all, the default, lists the whole covered catalog, which can start with games the provider still holds open weeks after kickoff. now lists what is on now: every game the provider reports in play (live or paused), plus any other game whose kickoff was at most 3 hours ago or is still to come; ended, postponed and cancelled games are left out, and a game with no published kickoff stays and sorts last. parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor. With a finished status, a page that spent its read budget carries a cursor past everything it read, which may be past the last game it returned. A cursor this endpoint did not issue returns 400 with error.param=cursor.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: sharp_money adds each game's sharp_money, the GameSharpMoney object GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug}/sharp-money returns, read from the sport board's cached aggregate: one board read per sport on the page, never a per-game compute. get.description: Every stored Polymarket market of one event_slug: the moneyline, spreads, totals, team totals, half and quarter lines, player props and the rest, plus the markets of the event's child events (a soccer game's exact score, halftime result and more-markets events), each with its own event_slug. The game object on GET /api/v1/games carries only the winner markets the sports board binds to the two sides; this read lists the rest. Each row carries the condition_id, the provider's sports_market_type, groupItemTitle and typed line, the outcome index the line belongs to when the provider states it, both outcome labels with their CLOB token ids, and active or closed status. families lists every market type the event holds with its counts, whatever the filters. Ordered by sports_market_type, then line, then condition_id. Live, upcoming and settled events all answer. expand=sharp_money adds each row's sharp-money split (side USD and S, A and B wallet counts per outcome) from the game page's per-line owner: computed for a line in the game's prop frame, not_computed for a line outside it (a player prop, a line beyond the seven around its family's main line, a closed or settled line), unavailable when the read failed or held no observation of the line within 120 ms. While the frame is being built, a line the game's stored split holds is computed and dated by money_as_of. Each read starts the game's split refilling: read again after a minute or two for the lines it could not answer. No price and no holder identity: GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug}/holders reads the holders of up to 25 of these markets in one call, and GET /api/v1/market/{condition_id}/holders or /snapshot reads one.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream of the live feed envelopes the platform already broadcasts (whale-trade pulses and other public/Pro feed events). Forwards the same backend-owned envelope shape as the internal feed; no provider data is recomputed. LiveScoreChanged frames may include optional live_score.tennis_points from API-Tennis in scoreboard order. This group has independent source_revision, observed_at, expires_at, set_number, and games; serving_side is omitted when unknown. Discard the group at expiry or set/game mismatch, and never compare its revision with the enclosing Polymarket score revision. Use event=LiveScoreChanged without market, wallet, grade, or size filters to receive these frames, which carry event_slug rather than condition_id. Authenticated via the oxi_sk Bearer key like every other /api/v1 endpoint, and limited to a small number of concurrent connections per API key and a cluster-wide ceiling across all keys (HTTP 429 with Retry-After when either cap is exceeded; HTTP 503 with Retry-After if a required Redis service is briefly unavailable). Each delivered frame carries an SSE id from one cluster-shared sequence that remains valid across backend replicas and process restarts. Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header (or the last_event_id / seq query fallback) to replay the missed window before resuming live. When the requested resume point is older than the retained window, ahead of the current sequence, separated from live delivery by an uncovered gap, or the server's sequence counter restarts mid-stream (a completeness.status of truncated, lagged, or reset), the stream emits a resync marker event (event: resync) instead of silently skipping frames. Idle connections receive periodic ': keep-alive' comment lines. This is a long-lived response: keep the connection open and read frames as they arrive. Authorization is re-checked for as long as the stream is open: checks become due every 30 seconds and the credential cache has a 10-second TTL. Body polling and lookup I/O can delay terminal delivery. A key that is revoked, expired or rotated, or an account that is deleted, locked or no longer subscribed, ends the stream with one terminal 'event: error' frame and then closes the connection. The frame's JSON is { type: 'error', error: <the same error object a reconnect is answered with: code, message, doc_url, reason, retry_at>, retry: <boolean> }; retry is false for every credential and account refusal (a reconnect is refused with the same 401, 402, 403 or 423), and true only when the credential store stopped answering (code rate_limit_unavailable with reason database_unavailable when protected-delivery grace expires 90 seconds after the last confirmed check; terminal arrival depends on body polling), in which case reconnect after the error's retry_at with Last-Event-ID set to the frame's id to resume. Replay uses the same ongoing authorization as live delivery. When a paused response resumes, due authorization and terminal controls run before another protected replay frame is emitted; bytes already handed to HTTP cannot be recalled. A healthy response paused beyond the grace period must complete one fresh check before protected delivery resumes. Compatible unexpired tennis_points survives temporary supplemental snapshot unavailability or contention; expiry and set/game mismatch still clear it.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Cluster-shared sequence id of the last frame the client successfully processed. The stream replays the strictly-newer retained window before resuming live, even when reconnect routing changes replicas. A future or expired id emits resync. Browser EventSource clients send this automatically on reconnect. Omit to attach live from now.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Query-string fallback for the Last-Event-ID resume cursor when the client cannot set the request header. Numeric cluster-shared sequence id; non-numeric or absent attaches live with no replay. A future or expired id emits resync.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: Alias for last_event_id. Numeric cluster-shared sequence id to resume after; non-numeric or absent attaches live with no replay. A future or expired id emits resync.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Optional per-connection subscribe-time filter. Comma-separated list of frame wire types (the SSE 'type' discriminator, e.g. WhaleTradesInserted,wallet_grade_changed); a frame passes only when its type is in the set. An unknown token returns HTTP 400 naming the offending value. An empty/all-whitespace value is treated as absent (no constraint). parameters.name: condition_id
parameters.description: Optional per-connection subscribe-time filter. Raw provider condition_id or mkt_-prefixed market id (normalized the same way the other v1 market endpoints normalize). A frame passes only when it carries a matching condition_id field; frames that carry no condition_id (e.g. whale-pulse events) are EXCLUDED while this is set. An empty value after normalization returns HTTP 400. Combines with event and min_grade as a logical AND; an absent param adds no constraint.

parameters.name: min_grade
parameters.description: Optional per-connection subscribe-time filter. A frame passes only when it carries a grade field whose grade is better-or-equal to this minimum (S is best). Frames without a grade (every frame except wallet_grade_changed and LargeTradeInsertedV2) are excluded. An invalid grade returns HTTP 400. Combines with the other filters as a logical AND.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Filter LargeTradeInsertedV2 frames to this Polymarket wallet. Other event types have no wallet and are excluded when set. Applied to live and retained Redis frames after privacy checks.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: Filter LargeTradeInsertedV2 frames to trades at or above this USD notional. Positive decimal with at most six places; other event types are excluded when set.

200.description: Open Server-Sent Events stream. schema.description:
Newline-delimited SSE frames: 'id: <seq>
data: <json-envelope>

id: <seq>
data: <json>

id: <seq>
data: <json>

' as the one terminal frame when the credential stops authorizing the stream, and ': keep-alive' comment lines while idle.

credentialRevoked.summary: Terminal error frame after the key was revoked mid-stream; the connection closes after it

402.description: Active Pro subscription required. The key is valid but the account has no active Pro subscription; error.reason is subscription_inactive and error.message names the reactivation URL (https://0xinsider.com/billing). Permanent until a person reactivates: no Retry-After, never retry on a schedule.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

get.description: Returns durable public large-trade events strictly after an opaque cursor, in commit order: events are ordered by the position at which their write became visible to every reader (whale_alerts.inserted_xid), then by whale_alerts.id, and a page never reaches past the oldest write transaction still open when it was read. A trade whose id is lower than one already delivered but whose write finished later is therefore delivered on a later request instead of being skipped (#16180). This is a separate API-key contract from the browser/session /api/events/feed stream: browser-only and private alert, following, radar, and position patch events are excluded until they have a durable public outbox. Carries large trades on sports and esports markets only (#27430).

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: condition_id
parameters.description: Only trades on this market: the raw provider condition_id or its mkt_-prefixed id. Bound to the cursor.

parameters.name: min_grade
parameters.description: Only trades by wallets at this grade or better (S best), read from the wallet's newest ranking at request time; a wallet with no grade never passes. Bound to the cursor.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: Only trades of at least this USD amount. Decimal and scientific query spellings normalize exactly to cents, rounding half away from zero; maximum 1e15 USD. Pass the dataset continuation decimal string unchanged to preserve the bound. Bound to the cursor.

parameters.name: expand

post.description: Creates a pending HTTPS webhook destination. The response includes one-time signing_secret and verification.token values. Deliveries are not sent until the endpoint is verified, and verification requires the destination to answer 2xx to a signed webhook.verification challenge (see POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/verify). The subscribable event_types and their data payload shapes are described by GET /api/v1/webhooks/events; the per-endpoint delivery log is GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries. Export lifecycle event types (export_job_ready, export_job_failed, export_job_expired, export_job_cancelled) are delivered only to the API-key account that created the export and contain no download URL; use the authorized export status and download routes. Four subscribable event types are Pro-only and only deliver to API keys on an active Pro subscription. whale_trades_inserted is one of them, gated by the same SubscriberScope::InsiderOnly mechanism as the other three (each type carries its own LiveEventContract entry; they share the scope value). The other three: wallet_grade_changed (data: wallet, trader_id, old_grade, new_grade, direction (upgrade|downgrade), skill_index, final_score, date) fires on a Pass-2 grade transition; insider_radar_flag_raised (data: trade_id, wallet, trader_id, condition_id, suspicion_score, track, side (yes|no), size, price) fires the first time a trade's suspicion score crosses the radar flag threshold; sharp_money_flow_detected (data: condition_id, net_flow_usd, abs_net_flow_usd, dominant_side (yes|no), grade_floor (S|A|B|C|D|F), whale_trade_count, window) fires when a scheduled scanner detects ranked-trader net flow crossing a threshold (up or down) on a market, and smart_money_flow_detected is its deprecated spelling of the same event. live_sports_updated (data: event_slug, game_id, league, version, changed, observed_at, published_at, status, period, clock, live, ended, scores, series_format, snapshot_url) is ungated and fires as a bounded per-game pulse when a live game's scores, status, period or live/ended state moves: at most one delivery per game per 20 seconds, with a live or ended transition exempt from that interval, and the game clock alone never firing one. version is a durable per-game ordinal, changed lists the material fields that moved since that game's previous delivered pulse, and snapshot_url is where to re-read the whole game after a gap. Delivery signing: each delivery request carries one or more HMAC-SHA256 signatures in the x-0xinsider-signature header as comma-separated v1=<hex> candidates. During staged rotation, the current and previous signing secrets are both signed for one hour; while 0xinsider rotates the key every signing secret is derived from, each also signs under the previous key, so the secret you hold keeps verifying. Up to four candidates; accept any valid candidate. Each candidate is HMAC-SHA256(signing_secret, "<timestamp>.<raw_request_body>"). The signed <timestamp> is sent separately as x-0xinsider-timestamp (unix seconds). To verify a delivery: read x-0xinsider-timestamp, reject it if it differs from the current time by more than 300 seconds, recompute each candidate over "<timestamp>.<raw_body>" with the active secrets, and compare using a constant-time comparison. Each delivery also carries x-0xinsider-event-id, x-0xinsider-event-type, x-0xinsider-delivery-id, and x-0xinsider-delivery-attempt headers. Retries and disabling: ordinary transient delivery failures use stable jitter between half and the existing 60, 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920 and 3600-second upper bounds (retry_policy.retry_horizon_seconds = 7380); on 408, 429, or 5xx, a valid Retry-After delta-seconds or HTTP-date replaces that one wait and is clamped to 60–3600 seconds, while missing, malformed, past, or non-retryable-response hints use the ordinary schedule. The delivery still has eight attempts (retry_policy.max_attempts), and an eighth failure becomes dead_letter. The delivery log exposes retry_schedule_reason and next_attempt_at so a receiver can see the active schedule. Separately, an endpoint is disabled after 8 consecutive failed attempts across all of its deliveries (retry_policy.disable_after_consecutive_failures); any successful attempt resets that count, so a busy endpoint that goes down can be disabled in minutes, well before any single delivery exhausts its retries. Disabling dead-letters every delivery still queued for the endpoint and emails the account owner, within about an hour, with each disabled endpoint and its last failed response. Re-enable it with PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/{id} {"enabled": true}; re-enabling does not resend dead-lettered deliveries. Resend each one with POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/redeliver, or catch up with GET /api/v1/events/feed/since from the last event you processed. GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries shows next_attempt_at and retry_schedule_reason for a delivery still waiting to retry.

post.description: Returns one dead_letter delivery to the delivery queue with a fresh attempt budget: status becomes pending, attempt_count resets to 0, and next_attempt_at is now, so the delivery worker claims it like any queued delivery, under the same per-owner and per-origin concurrency limits. Use it after a failed delivery exhausts its retries, or after re-enabling an endpoint whose queued deliveries were dead-lettered when it was disabled: PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/{id} {"enabled": true} resends nothing by itself. The resend is signed with the endpoint's current signing secret and sent to its current URL, and keeps the delivery's event_id and idempotency-key header, so a receiver that already processed the event can deduplicate it; x-0xinsider-delivery-attempt starts again at 1. last_response_status and last_error keep the previous failure until the next attempt records its own. Returns 409 when the delivery is already delivered or still queued (pending, retry, or processing), or when the endpoint would not receive it (disabled, not verified, or no longer subscribed to the delivery's event_type); error.message names the step that lets the same request succeed. Returns 404 for an endpoint or delivery the caller does not own, including a delivery removed by the seven-day retention of delivered and dead_letter history.

post.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Streamable HTTP transport. Accepts one JSON-RPC 2.0 request or notification. ID-bearing initialize, ping, tools/list, and tools/call requests (and server/discover on revision 2026-07-28) receive one same-ID JSON-RPC response; an unknown method, or a notification method sent with an id, answers JSON-RPC error -32601. Every ID-less message (a notification, known or not) receives HTTP 202 with no body and runs nothing; an unsolicited response message receives HTTP 400 with a JSON-RPC -32600 body and no id. Unknown cancellation IDs are ignored; cancellation does not stop running tool work. Only tools/call is counted against the per-minute request budget, the monthly quota and pay-as-you-go usage; every other message, with or without a key, spends none of them and reports the per-IP budget in RateLimit-* (since 2026-10-18). Remote MCP exposes 55 read-only tools for public V1 read operations: get_leaderboard, get_trader, batch_get_traders, get_large_trades, get_large_trade, get_large_trades_history, get_whale_trades, get_whale_trade, get_whale_trades_history, get_edge_hunter, list_games, get_game, get_market_flow, batch_get_market_flow, get_market_intel, batch_get_market_intel, get_sharp_money_flows, get_smart_money_flows, get_market_snapshot, get_suspicious_trades, get_suspicious_trade, get_insider_radar, get_insider_radar_flag, get_positions, get_position_timeline, get_position_timeline_by_id, search_markets, search_content, explore_markets, get_event_replay_since, list_webhooks, get_webhook, get_daily_report_snapshot, get_weekly_report_snapshot, get_monthly_report_snapshot, get_report, get_trader_export_snapshot, get_coverage, get_platforms, get_large_positions, get_trending_wallets, get_trader_pnl, get_pick_of_the_day, get_pick_of_the_day_ledger_entry, get_pick_of_the_day_archive, get_trader_context, get_trader_categories, get_trader_grade_at, get_market_holders, get_market_candles, get_combo_fills, get_combos_summary, get_combo, get_large_trade_counterparty_executions, get_large_trade_counterparty_makers. Webhook create/update/delete/verify/rotate operations are intentionally not exposed as remote MCP tools. The remote endpoint advertises tools only; it does not implement resources/list, resources/read, prompts/list, or prompts/get. Each tool dispatches to the matching /api/v1/* handler in-process so auth, rate limits, and payload shape match. initialize, notifications/initialized, ping and tools/list answer without a credential; tools/call (and any GET) need Authorization: Bearer <token> with an OAuth 2.1 access token (see the oauth2 security scheme; a tool outside the token's scopes returns isError) or an API key, and without one answer HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge whose resource_metadata names the RFC 9728 document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1/mcp. A key in a ?token= query parameter is rejected on every authenticated route (the public routes ignore it) with 401 invalid_api_key and error.reason api_key_in_query, because URLs land in shell history, browser history, and logs; a client that can only take a URL can run the @0xinsider/mcp stdio package. The endpoint is stateless: it mints no Mcp-Session-Id and ignores one a client sends. Origin header, when present, is validated against the 0xinsider + localhost allowlist. tools/call arguments are validated against the tool's advertised inputSchema before anything runs: an unknown key, a wrong type, an out-of-range number, a value outside an enum or an argument combination outside a oneOf answers a tool result with isError true whose text names the field, never a query built from the arguments that fit; a tools/call without name, or whose arguments is not an object, answers JSON-RPC error -32602 and runs nothing. Every tools/call result carries the REST envelope's meta verbatim (request_id, cached, cache_age_s, cost, and the route's provenance such as source and completeness on get_whale_trades_history or ranking_source and directional_source on get_edge_hunter) as structuredContent.meta beside the payload's own keys, and a tool failure carries structuredContent.error with the REST error fields verbatim (code, reason, param, doc_url, retry_at) plus retry_after_seconds, request_id and status, beside its text. The MCP-Protocol-Version request header is checked on every POST: a value outside 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 answers HTTP 400 with the standard error envelope (error.code bad_request); an absent header is served as 2025-03-26, the transport specification's compatibility default. Revision 2026-07-28 also requires the Mcp-Method header (JSON-RPC error -32020 without it) and adds resultType to every result. Browser preflight allows MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name.

(2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. Until 2026-09-22 an authenticated GET answered 200 text/event-stream and closed the body at once, which conforming clients reconnected to every second. Every JSON-RPC request goes over POST. Since 2026-10-18 the authenticated 405 spends no per-minute request, monthly quota or pay-as-you-go usage, and reports the per-IP budget in RateLimit-*.

get.description: One UTC day of resolved sports and esports markets: how often the side the profitable (S, A and B grade) wallets held won, beside how often every qualifying wallet's side won, one vote each. `markets` lists each market they held a position in, with the consensus side, its confidence, and the full roster of wallets, their side, cost and realized P&L; `view=totals` drops it. Counts cover the whole day before that list is filtered. A past day is served from its retained build: `generated_at` says when it was built and `source_updates_pending` that a newer build has been requested. 503 read_model_warming while the day has no build yet; one has been requested.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

503.description: Service unavailable. On this route a 503 has TWO distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="read_model_warming": the requested endpoint cannot serve its read model yet. Exact causes are endpoint-specific and can include a cold or contended refresh or a dependency that prevented refresh; consult that endpoint's contract and do not infer dependency health from this shared reason. This is endpoint-local unavailability, not rate limiting: retry only this route after Retry-After (or error.retry_at), and do not feed it into a rate-limit backoff shared with other endpoints. (2) no error.reason: the Redis-backed authenticated rate limiter is unavailable and the middleware failed closed; Retry-After is the seconds until it probes Redis again. Both carry error.code="rate_limit_unavailable" (a FROZEN contract value, so it cannot be split per cause) and X-Request-Id -- which is why error.reason, not error.code, is the discriminator.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until retrying is worth doing. With error.reason="read_model_warming" this is the endpoint-local read-model retry interval; without a reason it is the rate-limiter outage cooldown. Always >= 1.

post.summary: Submit a trader dataset export job
post.description: Queues an async export of the trader's full dataset in the requested format (json default, ndjson, or csv) and returns the job resource. Poll the status route at poll_after_s until terminal is true, then follow the download route while status is 'ready' (until expires_at, 24 hours from submit). Reuse: without fresh=true, a live job for the same trader and format inside its retention window (queued, running, reconcile_required or ready) is returned with 200 instead of a new one, except a job its owner asked to cancel, which is never reused; its data_as_of says what its file is a snapshot of. With fresh=true only a queued job (which has not started reading) is reused; a running, reconciling or ready job is left alone and a new job is reserved, which consumes quota like any new job. Both decisions run under one per-account lock, so two concurrent submits cannot both reserve when one would have reused the other. Quotas are the per-user daily and per-address hourly export caps, keyed on the API key owner so an API key never widens its owner's quota. New full exports select one database read generation before delivery. JSON and NDJSON add export_metadata.generation (id, selected_at, consistency=repeatable_read, source_watermarks for positions, native P&L, categories and all matching trades), position_generation, provider_observations (provider values and observation/revision metadata), category_data_as_of, pnl_date_from/to, pnl_rows, pnl_row_limit (3650), markets_rows, markets_row_limit (50000), summary_basis and trades_basis. Summary counts cover all stored markets; the markets section retains its existing latest-activity 50000-row limit and P&L its earliest-3650-days limit. These are database consistency and section coverage facts, not a claim that providers observed every section simultaneously. CSV appends export_generation, export_selected_at and export_consistency columns. Downloaded objects also expose x-amz-meta-export-generation, x-amz-meta-export-selected-at, x-amz-meta-export-consistency, x-amz-meta-export-trades and x-amz-meta-export-provenance headers, including empty CSV files. Historical artifacts remain unchanged. Select CSV columns by name; JSON/NDJSON readers may ignore the additive fields. A read exceeding 600 seconds or an uncompressed artifact exceeding 2 GiB fails without publishing a partial file.

get.description: Returns the job resource for a submitted export: status (queued | running | cancel_requested | reconcile_required | ready | failed | expired | cancelled), terminal, next_action and poll_after_s, the lifecycle timestamps, the retention window (expires_at) and, once the file is written, data_as_of and the artifact identity. A ready job past expires_at reads expired; a queued, running or reconciling job past expires_at reads failed. Work stops at retention safe points; completion and reconciliation cannot publish ready after expiry. The failure event carries failure_reason expired_before_completion and next_action resubmit; delivery never extends retention. A running job its owner cancelled reads cancel_requested until the worker stops, then cancelled. failed, cancelled and expired jobs stay readable for 48 hours, then 404.

post.description: Cancels a submitted export and returns the job resource, the same shape the status route returns. A queued job reads cancelled at once and no worker will start it. A running job reads cancel_requested until the worker reaches its next safe point, then cancelled: the worker checks every 5 seconds while it reads the snapshot and between upload parts, and once more at the last point before the file is published; a storage request already in flight finishes first (each is bounded at 120 seconds), and a partial upload is discarded. If the worker itself stops first, the job reads cancelled as that worker shuts down for a deploy, and otherwise within a minute of its 30-minute lease lapsing. A job a cancel can no longer reach is returned unchanged with 200: once its upload is being completed it finishes as ready (or reconcile_required, then ready or failed), and ready, failed, expired and cancelled jobs are terminal. A cancel never deletes a ready file; compare status before and after. Repeating the request is safe: it converges on the same state and never repeats a transition, so a client that lost the answer can send it again or read the status route. While terminal is false, poll the status route after poll_after_s. Quota is unchanged: the submit's reservation keeps counting toward the per-user daily and per-address hourly export caps for its full window, as a failed export's does, and a job its owner asked to cancel is never reused by a later submit, which reserves a new job. Webhook endpoints subscribed to export_job_cancelled receive it when the job reaches cancelled. An unknown job id, or a job owned by another account or submitted for another trader, answers 404 exactly as the status route does.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

Window and filters freeze on admission; rows and source facts freeze on one worker database snapshot. NDJSON uses exact decimal strings, with no current grade or market enrichment. Sports and esports markets only (#27430): trades on any other market are left out of the file, and a condition_id naming such a market returns 404 not_found with error.reason market_out_of_scope before any job is reserved.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

post.description: Additive asynchronous consent flow; the legacy POST /verify keeps its synchronous 200/422 behavior and retry policy. Commits one durable attempt and returns 202 without awaiting DNS or the receiver. Send the original verification_token. Optional Idempotency-Key replays the original admission response for the same endpoint/token identity; a changed request returns 422 and an in-flight matching key returns 409. Different keys for the same token revision recover the same attempt, including terminal attempts, without new receiver work. Poll status_url for current state; 202 is admission, not activation. A supervised worker sends the existing signed webhook.verification body with an additional verification_attempt_id and x-0xinsider-verification-attempt header, stable across at-least-once retries. Verify the timestamp/raw-body HMAC and answer 2xx. DNS is public-address-pinned; redirects and proxies are refused and response bodies are not read. Timeout/transport/429/5xx failures retry at most 4 attempts, with 5/15/45-second waits, until the earlier token deadline or 15-minute horizon. Other receiver statuses and URL/security refusals are terminal. Activation requires current owner eligibility, endpoint/token/URL/signing identity, unexpired attempt/token and valid lease. Configuration changes or disable/delete cancel obsolete work. Terminal ciphertext is erased; status exposes no token, signing secret, address or receiver body. History is available for 7 days.

get.description: Returns live Polymarket combo taker fills with exact decimal-string economics, wallet identities, grades, legs, conjunction results, and ingest coverage. Requires an active Pro or Max API key. Listing includes executions with price at most 0.95; use combo detail for complete history. Sports and esports only (#27449): a fill is listed only when every leg of its combo is a sports or esports market; a combo with a leg on any other market never appears, and filters, page sizes and continuations apply after that exclusion. Recent ordering uses an exclusive cursor; largest and payout use offsets. Continuations are based on page fullness and may lead to an empty final page.

parameters.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. parameters.description: CSV of pending, won, or lost; all clears the filter. Unknown results appear only in unfiltered lists.

parameters.name: legs
parameters.description: CSV of 2, 3, 4, or 5+; all clears the filter. A combo matches any named pick count.

parameters.name: min_stake
parameters.description: Minimum collateral in whole USDC.

parameters.name: min_multiplier
parameters.description: 0 disables the filter; otherwise use 2..1000000. Minimum shares per dollar at execution.

parameters.name: grades
parameters.description: CSV of S, A, B, C, D, F; all clears the filter. Ungraded wallets do not match.

parameters.name: sports
parameters.description: CSV of nfl, ncaaf, nba, wnba, baseball, hockey, soccer, tennis, table-tennis, esports, mma, boxing, golf, cricket, f1, pickleball; all clears the filter. Matches when any leg belongs to a selected sport.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Recent is newest first; largest ranks collateral; payout ranks buy-fill shares and excludes sells.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Defaults to all for recent and 24h for largest or payout.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Integer values outside the range are clamped to 1..200.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Exclusive block_number:log_index cursor for recent only; send the returned next_cursor unchanged.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Offset for ranked largest or payout ordering; use returned next_offset.

get.description:
Max-only canonical Edge Hunter API with board, signals and observations views. An active Pro credential receives 403 forbidden with reason max_plan_required. Default board admission and ordering remain compatible: B grade floor, 30-row cap, 48-hour kickoff horizon, full Max projection and both current outcome quotes. Board outcomes include nullable token_id; the full signal includes nullable backed token_id, ranked_at copied from the frozen signal_created_at, and the existing aggregate category_skill evidence. Quote ts/validated_at and metadata_updated_at retain their separate meanings; none is wallet entry cost. Board quotes read verified display-price and websocket caches only, with no inline provider request or request-triggered REST refresh. Uncached outcomes remain null; retained quotes keep their original observation clock and existing retention bound. Board category, min_grade and limit are configurable; horizon clamps 1..48 and cap clamps 1..30. total counts selected admitted rows before the cap.

Signals exposes full ranked records and category-skill/source evidence with default B grade floor, 12-hour horizon (clamp 1..48), page limit 20 (clamp 1..100) and cursor. Observations requires wider_holder, in_play or emerging_pile and retains full records, verified token IDs, midpoint price marks, holder/provider/directional clocks, snapshot_as_of, degraded, degradation_reasons, coverage and source-generation/category funnel evidence. Required degradation_reasons records each operational cause with canonical sport or null for generation-wide evidence, and is empty only for a healthy generation. For sports and esports reads, the first four coverage counts stay global across cohort/category/selectors; selected_observations counts matching rows before pagination and returned_observations equals data.length. An unmappable legacy category retains its zero-work empty generation with all coverage counts zero and no degradation reasons, without reading the all-sports cache. Intentional capacity_limited input, the one-page holder bound (holder_scan_complete=false, counted in coverage.incomplete_holder_markets) and board_upcoming_status=not_configured do not by themselves degrade a generation. Reconciled terminals prove accounting, not complete holder coverage. Observation horizon stays 48 hours with 12-hour in-play kickoff lookback and 30-second live snapshot ceiling. In-play additionally requires a coherent nonfuture original live-source clock no older than 30 seconds at publication and every served reuse; compute and missed-pass grace never renew that clock. Provider-confirmed live membership is observed independently of rendered scores, quotes and holder enrichment. UI refresh-marker expiry or score invalidation alone does not invalidate a separately observed provider membership. Explicit provider-source invalidation or an invalid, incomplete, future, expired or missing source remains unavailable. When one scheduled observation refresh misses its deadline, other cohorts may keep serving the last snapshot for up to 45 more seconds, with its age in meta.cache_age_s and its completion time in snapshot_as_of; a second missed refresh in a row returns 503 read_model_warming. An expired in-play source returns 503 read_model_warming even within generation grace. Funnel diagnostics describe the warmed generation/category accounting rather than the selected league/type/ID input census. admission=most_held_48h with cohort=wider_holder opts in to the most-held selection instead of the default one: per sport, up to 8 markets kicking off within 48 hours, most graded holders first, then volume, then soonest kickoff, at most 4 per event, recomputed every refresh; every row carries admitted_by most_held_48h, the response echoes admission, and funnel, coverage and degradation describe that selection. Both wider_holder selections add departures: the markets whose card left that selection before kickoff, each with departed_at, the departed card's last_observed_at and a reason from the funnel's terminal vocabulary, so a reader can tell a move to view=signals (primary_slate_candidate) from a split holder pile. Every observations snapshot names in signals_as_of the view=signals snapshot whose listed markets it excluded from wider_holder. A sport's pregame wider_holder holders are read only while a wider_holder or emerging_pile request named that sport, or named no category, within the last 30 minutes (default and most_held_48h counted apart; in-play reads never pause). A request whose sport was not read, or one without a category while any sport was not, returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After: 45 and restarts those reads; the retry serves the same rows as before, and that sport's admitted markets count as capacity_limited in the global coverage counts while they were not read.

Every view accepts kind, sports, leagues, market_types, condition_ids, event_slugs, series_slugs and legacy category. Repeat array query keys or supply comma-separated values inside a key; at most 100 supplied values per axis before deduplication. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate. Lists match OR and axes match AND. Sports and machine leagues normalize case-insensitively; market_types/event_slugs/series_slugs remain trimmed exact case-sensitive provider strings. category=NFL reaches Football, while leagues=nfl selects NFL only. Selection runs before cap/pagination, binds advanced cursors/ETags, and is echoed in optional top-level selection whenever a selector or nonblank category is requested. Missing selected metadata excludes a row. Unknown well-formed market IDs or provider identities return empty results.

Each row adds required nullable market_context for authoritative discovery. A frozen observed sidecar gives required nullable league, series_slug, market_type and metadata_updated_at; a pre-selector cached generation can yield context:null on an unselected read. metadata_updated_at is exactly local market_canonical.updated_at, never a provider observation clock or current-time fallback. A selected read without sidecar readiness returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After: 5, never silently wider results. SDK selected reads enforce strict query validation and require the echo.

All public views read warmed generations only; missing or stale readiness returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After: 5. Advanced views use private,no-cache with ETag/If-None-Match/304; no request holder/provider computation. Default board has no ETag/pagination and private,no-store. Invalid view-specific parameters return 400. Replaced snapshots or changed cursor-bound filters return cursor_expired. Price marks are market midpoints, not wallet entry cost; volume is provider taker shares. Nullable/omitted evidence and db_only/degraded provenance remain explicit. Analytics is not an execution instruction.

parameters.name: X-Query-Validation
parameters.description: Set to strict to reject unsupported query names. By default, unknown query names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Conditional validator for view=signals or view=observations only. A semantic match returns 304 with no body. The default board does not emit ETag or return 304.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Response mode. board preserves the full quoted board; signals exposes ranked records and category evidence; observations exposes cohort measurements and accountable funnel evidence. Defaults to board.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Legacy canonical bucket alias, now accepted in every view. Provider aliases canonicalize: NFL reaches Football and EPL reaches Soccer. Use leagues for a league-specific selection. An unmappable non-sport category returns an empty result and echoes category non_sport. Combines with other selection axes using AND.

parameters.name: cohort
parameters.description: Required for view=observations; wider_holder, in_play or emerging_pile. Rejected for board and signals. wider_holder covers pregame markets that view=signals does not list at its widest selection (horizon_hours=48, min_grade=B, no selector), so until kickoff a market is read in one view or the other. A market view=signals lists leaves wider_holder as primary_slate_candidate, and is a wider_holder candidate again in the first refresh after view=signals stops listing it; signals_as_of names the view=signals snapshot each refresh read. Each refresh evaluates at most 8 markets per sport and cohort, wider_holder by soonest kickoff (most graded holders first among equal kickoffs) and in_play by most graded holders, so a market among a sport's 8 soonest stays evaluated until its game starts. wider_holder also evaluates up to 8 more markets per sport that kick off within 24 hours, most graded holders first, so the most-held markets appear up to a day before kickoff. Each of these keeps its place in later refreshes until its game starts while its holder page still shows a card or could not be read, so a more-held market waits for a free place instead of displacing it. Each row's admitted_by names its place, most_held or soonest_kickoff. The rest count in coverage.capacity_limited_markets. Emerging pile is a wider-holder projection with sharp_pct in [0.75,0.85), complete holder scans and future kickoff, not an independent population or arrival history.

parameters.name: admission
parameters.description: Opt-in admission rule for view=observations with cohort=wider_holder; rejected for every other view and cohort. most_held_48h returns the most-held selection instead of the default one: per sport, up to 8 wider_holder markets kicking off within 48 hours, most graded holders first, then most volume, then soonest kickoff, at most 4 per event. It is recomputed every refresh and keeps no place, so a more-held market displaces a less-held one; markets view=signals lists stay excluded. Every row carries admitted_by most_held_48h, including a market the default selection also evaluates, and the response echoes admission. funnel, coverage, degraded and degradation_reasons describe this selection: a wider_holder candidate it did not take counts as capacity_limited. Its markets that no default place covers are read after every default market, at most once per 10 minutes, so a row can rest on a holder page up to 15 minutes old (holder_snapshot_at). Omit for the default selection. Cursors and ETags bind it.

parameters.name: min_grade
parameters.description: Board and signals: S, A or B, default B. Requires a piled-side holder at the selected grade floor or better, without removing other holders. Rejected for observations.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Board row cap defaults to 30 and clamps integer values to 1..30; total counts selected admitted rows before the cap. Signals and observations page size defaults to 20 and clamps to 1..100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque canonical Edge Hunter cursor from next_cursor. Bound to view, every normalized selection axis, grade/horizon where applicable, source snapshot and ordering; observations also bind cohort, admission and emerging cutoff. Changed selections or replaced snapshots return cursor_expired. Rejected in board.

parameters.name: horizon_hours
parameters.description: Kickoff window for board (default 48) or signals (default 12). Integer values clamp to 1..48. Rejected for observations, whose pre-game universe is fixed at 48 hours with a 12-hour in-play kickoff lookback.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: All views: sports excludes the Esports bucket; esports selects only Esports. Omit for both. Combines with other selections using AND. Selected reads echo normalized selection and require frozen metadata readiness.

parameters.name: sports
parameters.description: Canonical sport buckets, including Esports and Table Tennis, matched case-insensitively. Unknown names and league aliases such as NFL are rejected in sports; use category for legacy bucket aliases or leagues for exact league selection. Omission covers every sport admitted by the selected view. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

parameters.name: leagues

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

Data calls require an active Pro subscription and return live data. A 401 carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.0xinsider.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" (RFC 6750 section 3, RFC 9728).

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE S256 for apps and MCP clients acting for a user. Public clients only (no client secret): register with RFC 7591 at https://api.0xinsider.com/oauth/register or present an https client ID metadata document URL as client_id. Authorization server metadata: https://api.0xinsider.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. The access token (oxi_at_..., one hour) is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; refresh tokens rotate on every use. A route outside the token's scopes answers 403 insufficient_scope. Walkthrough: https://0xinsider.com/auth.md.

scopes.read: Read markets, traders, large trades, positions, reports, search, the event stream and every MCP tool
scopes.webhooks: Create, list, verify, rotate and delete webhook endpoints
scopes.export: Start, poll and download trader exports
scopes.usage: Read the caller's API usage counters

WebhookEventIdHeader.name: x-0xinsider-event-id
WebhookEventIdHeader.description: The event id, equal to the body `id`.

WebhookEventTypeHeader.name: x-0xinsider-event-type
WebhookEventTypeHeader.description: The event type the endpoint registered, equal to the body `type`.

WebhookIdempotencyKeyHeader.name: idempotency-key
WebhookIdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Stable key of this logical delivery (`whdel_...`). Every retry repeats it, so deduplicate on it.

WebhookDeliveryIdHeader.name: x-0xinsider-delivery-id
WebhookDeliveryIdHeader.description: Numeric id of this delivery, as a decimal string.

WebhookDeliveryAttemptHeader.name: x-0xinsider-delivery-attempt
WebhookDeliveryAttemptHeader.description: The delivery attempt counter, as a decimal string.

WebhookTimestampHeader.name: x-0xinsider-timestamp
WebhookTimestampHeader.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was signed. Reject a delivery whose timestamp is more than 300 seconds from your clock.

WebhookSignatureHeader.name: x-0xinsider-signature
WebhookSignatureHeader.description: `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{raw body}` under the endpoint signing secret. During a staged secret rotation, or while 0xinsider rotates the key every signing secret is derived from, it carries up to four comma-separated `v1=` candidates, the current secret's first: accept the delivery when any one verifies.

WebhookId.name: id
WebhookId.description: Webhook endpoint id owned by the authenticated API key user.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional safe-retry key. Reuse the same value only when retrying the exact same mutation request body; a different body returns 422 and an in-flight matching request returns 409.

X-Query-Validation.name: X-Query-Validation
X-Query-Validation.description: Opt into strict query-name validation. The default is compatible: unknown names are ignored and reported in X-Query-Ignored. With strict, an unknown name returns 400 bad_request with error.reason unknown_query_parameter before the handler runs, including when its percent escape is incomplete.

LargeTradeSubscriptionFilters.description: All present fields narrow large_trade_inserted_v2 delivery. Grade is observed at publication; ungraded trades do not match min_grade. An empty object matches every large trade.

condition_id.description: Raw provider condition ID or mkt_-prefixed market ID.

wallet.description: Polymarket wallet address; matching is case-insensitive.

min_grade.description: S is best; ungraded trades do not match.

min_size_usd.description: Positive USD notional as an exact decimal string.

retry_horizon_seconds.description: Total wait from a delivery's first failed attempt to its last retry: 60, 120, 240, 480, 960, 1920 and 3600 seconds. A delivery still failing after that is dead_letter.

disable_after_consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive failed attempts, across all of this endpoint's deliveries, after which the endpoint is disabled and its queued deliveries are dead-lettered. Any successful attempt resets the count.

token.description: One-time verification token returned only on create or URL change. Pass it to POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/verify, which activates the endpoint only when the destination also answers the signed webhook.verification challenge with a 2xx.

WebhookEventDescriptor.description: Self-describing entry in the webhook event catalog: the event type a subscriber lists in event_types, when it fires, the data payload shape, and whether it currently fires (active) or is reserved (dormant, subscribable but not yet delivered). Pro-only event types (large_trades_inserted, whale_trades_inserted, wallet_grade_changed, suspicious_trade_flagged, insider_radar_flag_raised, sharp_money_flow_detected, smart_money_flow_detected) only deliver to API keys on an active Pro subscription. Export lifecycle event types (export_job_ready, export_job_failed, export_job_expired, export_job_cancelled) are owner-scoped to the API-key account that created the export and contain no download URL; use the authorized export status/download routes. Some entries are two spellings of one event: large_trades_inserted and whale_trades_inserted, trader_synced and whale_trader_synced, suspicious_trade_flagged and insider_radar_flag_raised, sharp_money_flow_detected and smart_money_flow_detected. Either spelling subscribes, and an endpoint receives deliveries under the spelling it registered. The deprecated spellings (whale_trades_inserted, whale_trader_synced, insider_radar_flag_raised, smart_money_flow_detected) reach their sunset on 2027-02-01 (#29352); register the canonical spelling.

description.description: One-line description of when the event fires.

payload_shape.description: Short description of the data payload object's shape.

status.description: active: the event has a firing producer callsite. dormant: advertised and subscribable, but does not yet enqueue any delivery.

WebhookDelivery.description: Owner-scoped view of one webhook delivery attempt. Deliberately omits the request body and the endpoint signing secret: a delivery log never re-exposes the payload or any secret material.

event_id.description: Stable event id for this delivery; identical across retries of the same logical event.

status.description: Delivery lifecycle state (e.g. pending, delivered, dead_letter).

attempt_count.description: Number of delivery attempts made so far.

last_response_status.description: HTTP status code of the most recent delivery attempt. Omitted until a response (or transport error) has been recorded.

last_error.description: Short description of the most recent delivery failure. Omitted when the last attempt succeeded or none has failed.

delivered_at.description: When the delivery was first accepted by the destination. Omitted until a delivery succeeds.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next delivery attempt is due, for a delivery whose status is pending or retry. null while an attempt is in flight (processing) and once the delivery is terminal (delivered or dead_letter).

retry_schedule_reason.description: Why next_attempt_at was scheduled: receiver_retry_after for an accepted Retry-After on a 408, 429, or 5xx response; transient_failure for a network or ordinary transient retry; permanent_or_auth_failure for another non-2xx response; manual_redelivery or configuration_changed for those queue actions. null while an attempt is in flight or once the delivery is terminal.

status.description: idle when no staged rotation exists, pending after prepare, and overlap after activate while both signing secrets are accepted.

overlap_expires_at.description: When the previous signing secret stops being emitted and accepted. null outside the overlap phase.

signing_secret.description: Returned only on create, immediate rotate-secret, staged rotate-secret/prepare, or staged rotate-secret/activate. Never returned by list, get, update, delete, verify, or retire.

url.description: Public HTTPS callback URL on the default port 443. Local, private, and internal targets are rejected, as is any explicit port other than 443 and any URL carrying credentials. Each user's URLs are unique after normalizing HTTPS scheme/host case, trailing DNS dots and port 443; path/query case is preserved. Pending verification and PATCH-disabled endpoints still reserve their stored URL. The destination must answer the signed webhook.verification challenge with a 2xx before POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/verify can activate the endpoint.

Replacement public HTTPS callback URL on the default port 443, validated and checked for uniqueness exactly like the create url. HTTPS scheme/host case, trailing DNS dots and port 443 normalize; path/query case is preserved. Changing it resets status to pending_verification and returns a new verification token; the new destination must pass the verification challenge before deliveries resume.

verification_token.description: The one-time token returned on create or on a url change. It is necessary but not sufficient: the destination must also answer the signed webhook.verification challenge with a 2xx.

Candle.description: One bucketed OHLC price candle. Prices are in provider [0, 1] units, truncated to 4 decimals at the rendering edge.

t.description: Bucket-start unix epoch (seconds): UTC midnight for 1d, the ISO-week Monday's UTC midnight for 1w.

o.description: Open price in provider [0, 1] units (first observed point in the bucket).

h.description: High price in provider [0, 1] units (max observed in the bucket).

l.description: Low price in provider [0, 1] units (min observed in the bucket).

c.description: Close price in provider [0, 1] units (last observed point in the bucket).

OutcomeCandles.description: One outcome token's bucketed candle series.

token_id.description: Provider CLOB token id the candles were read for.

candles.description: OHLC candles for this outcome token, ascending by bucket start.

MarketCandles.description: Provider-first bucketed OHLC price candles for a market's outcome tokens, derived from our stored copy of the Polymarket CLOB prices-history series (covers open and resolved markets).

condition_id.description: Market condition id the candles were read for.

resolution.description: Bucketing granularity that produced these candles.

outcomes.description: One entry per present provider token (YES first, then NO); empty when no tokens have been fetched yet.

MarketWalletsInOut.description: One market's net buyers and net sellers over a 24h or 7d window, as the market page's wallets in/out panel shows a Pro viewer.

condition_id.description: The market's raw provider condition id.

window.description: The window the nets are summed over: 24h or 7d.

window_start.description: The window's inclusive start; null only when the bounds are unknown.

window_end.description: The window's inclusive end, the read's clock; null only when the bounds are unknown.

summary.description: Totals over every wallet that traded the market in the window, not only the listed 50.

wallets_in.description: Wallets with a positive net in the window.

wallets_out.description: Wallets with a negative net in the window.

net_usd.description: The sum of every wallet's net, in USD. A fully rotated wallet nets zero and is on neither side.

net_buyers.description: Wallets whose net is positive, largest first, at most 25.

items.description: One wallet's net in the window.

display_name.description: The name the site shows: the 0xinsider username, else the shortened address.

grade.description: Today's grade; null for an ungraded or untracked wallet.

net_usd.description: Buys minus sells in the window, both outcomes, in USD: the matched notional, fees excluded.

last_traded_at.description: The wallet's newest trade on any market, at or before window_end; null when unknown.

net_sellers.description: Wallets whose net is negative, most negative first, at most 25.

items.description: One wallet's net in the window.

display_name.description: The name the site shows: the 0xinsider username, else the shortened address.

grade.description: Today's grade; null for an ungraded or untracked wallet.

net_usd.description: Buys minus sells in the window, both outcomes, in USD: the matched notional, fees excluded.

last_traded_at.description: The wallet's newest trade on any market, at or before window_end; null when unknown.

Game.description: One sports or esports game: both sides, its schedule, provider status, its winner markets (the moneyline, or the soccer 1X2 legs) with their available provider moneyline price states and liquidity, and the game's traded volume. The event's other markets are on GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug}/markets. Assembled from the same provider-first live and upcoming projections the site's boards use, with no request-time provider fan-out.

event_slug.description: The game's identity, for example mlb-mil-cin-2026-06-22. The same key the live_sports_updated webhook pulse carries and the same key /api/v1/games/{event_slug} takes.

game_id.description: The provider's Gamma gameId, as a string. Omitted when the canonical owner has no single value for this slug: the provider stamps one gameId across an event's derivative siblings, so an ambiguous read is reported as unknown rather than guessed.

sport.description: The canonical sport bucket, for example Soccer or Table Tennis. Omitted when neither the board scope nor the provider category names one.

league.description: The league tag, for example nfl or epl. Omitted for a sport served as one whole bucket with no league scope.

title.description: The provider's event title. Omitted when the provider sent none.

scheduled_at.description: Kickoff in UTC, as the provider supplied it. Omitted when the provider published none; coverage.schedule then reads unavailable.

competitors.description: Both sides, in the provider's own order. For a team league the provider lists the home side first. Empty when the provider identified neither side.

series_format.description: The esports series length, for example Bo3. Omitted for everything else.

draw_offered.description: Whether this read includes a market classified as paying on a draw, including soccer's independent 1X2 draw leg. Read this instead of assuming a two-outcome moneyline.

markets.description: The game's winner markets the sports board binds to its sides (the moneyline, or a soccer game's three 1X2 legs), ordered by condition_id. Spreads, totals, period lines and props are on GET /api/v1/games/{event_slug}/markets.

volume.description: The game's traded volume, the figure the sports board carries for it, with its source, basis, unit and observation clock. A client can rank or filter games by volume.value. Omitted when the board carries no volume for the game, and on a finished game read from its stored record (freshness.source stored); never 0 in place of a missing figure.

GameVolume.description: A game's traded volume as Polymarket reports it, read by the sports board with no request-time provider call. A one-side taker share count, the number Polymarket's own pages print behind a dollar sign, not the cash that changed hands.

value.description: The volume at full precision, in unit.

unit.description: taker_shares: cumulative one-side taker volume in shares. One share pays $1 at settlement, so this is not cash traded. Omitted only on a figure observed before units were recorded; never assume cash.

basis.description: game_lines: the game volume Polymarket's game page states, summed over the game's own lines. event_total: the whole event's volume, stated when no game volume was readable. The two can differ in either direction. Omitted when the basis is unknown.

source.description: The Polymarket API the figure was read from: polymarket_data (the Data API's live volume) or gamma (the Gamma API).

observed_at.description: When 0xinsider read the figure from the provider, never a provider-authored timestamp. Omitted when no read time is held for it.

fresh_for_seconds.description: How long after observed_at 0xinsider treats the figure as current: 60 or 300 by source and basis, or 3600 for an older figure kept because a later read of the same total was lower or missing (a cumulative volume never falls).

GameSharpMoney.description: Event-level sharp money for one game. Every aggregate field is null unless status is computed; null means unknown, never zero.

GameStatus.description: Where the game is in its own life, as the provider reports it. A postponement, a cancellation and a suspension each keep their own state, so a client can tell a game that will be played later from one that never will be.

state.description: scheduled: kickoff is ahead, or the provider still lists the game open and neither in play nor ended. With no live-score frame a game stays scheduled past its kickoff until the provider says otherwise. live: the provider reports it in play. paused: halftime or a provider-reported break. ended: the provider reported a final, an award or a forfeit. postponed, cancelled, suspended, delayed: the provider's own verdict, kept distinct. A tennis match that the provider still lists in play, with no live score feed and no change of period or score for 3 hours, also reads suspended. unknown: no provider state reached this read. A kickoff in the past is never read as live on its own.

match_status.description: The provider status folded onto one vocabulary across leagues. unknown means the provider sent a value this API has no meaning for; provider_status keeps that value verbatim. Omitted when no live-score frame carries a status, as for a listed game no live-score feed has reported yet.

provider_status.description: The live-score feed's status string, verbatim. Omitted when no live-score frame carries one. This API never puts a label of its own here, such as Scheduled for a listed game.

period.description: The provider's period label, for example Q3, End Q2 or T5. Omitted when the provider sent none.

clock.description: The game clock as the provider spells it, never reformatted. Omitted when the provider sent none.

live.description: Whether the game is in play. It is the provider's own in-play flag, except that three cases read false: a game the provider reports suspended (period SUS), a game rescheduled to a later kickoff, and a tennis match that the provider still lists in play with no live score feed and no change of period or score for 3 hours. Omitted when no live-score frame exists, which is not the same as false.

ended.description: Whether the game is over. Always present.

name.description: The competitor's name as the provider gives it.

provider_id.description: The provider's league-scoped competitor id, as a string. Omitted when the provider has not identified this side; coverage.competitors then reads labels.

logo.description: Provider crest or logo URL. Omitted when there is none.
