holder_scan_complete.description: True only when the provider page read for each outcome token listed every holder of that token. Observation collection reads one 100-row page per token; a token with more holders stays incomplete. False means holder counts and dollar totals measure the observed positive-holder subset. sharp_pct describes that observed subset and is not a lower bound on the full-population percentage. Incomplete scans cannot satisfy a future capital-promotion gate.

holder_snapshot_at.description: Proven provider holder observation time. A warm cache hit uses only the original provider completion time from its companion metadata, never cache-read time. A wider_holder or emerging_pile row whose holder read did not finish or failed in the current pass may reuse that market's last pregame holder page for up to 15 minutes; an in_play row may reuse its last in-play page, read after the provider reported the game live and never before that market's own kickoff, for up to 10 minutes. Both ages are counted when the snapshot is computed. Either reuse carries that page's original time here and provider_read_source cached. A pregame market more than an hour before kickoff reuses its last page the same way until that page is 10 minutes old, and only then is read again; while that market has had no trade since the page, it keeps reusing the page until it is 30 minutes old. Once that market's own kickoff has passed, an in_play row with provider_read_source cached, a warm hit or a reuse, never carries a page read before it. Null, malformed, future, or stale holder time fails in-play closed.

directional_status.description: Truthful state of the directional read, which classifies each graded holder by its fresh synced legs across the game's markets and, when holder_scan_complete is true, by Polymarket's currentValue on both outcomes of this market. A wider_holder row can remain emitted with unavailable and terminal wider_holder_emitted; in_play fails closed instead and terminates as in_play_directional_unavailable.

directional_rank_score.description: Recorded side ordering score; higher values sort first.

rank.description: 1-based rank within this observation cohort and snapshot.

market_context.description: Required nullable frozen metadata context. Null only during the legacy-generation transition; selected reads require sidecar readiness and fail closed with 503 instead.

EdgeHunterFunnelReport.description: Per-sport accountable funnel for the full observation snapshot, returned on every page.

EdgeHunterSportFunnelReport.description: Independent sports-board supply plus stored-universe terminal accounting for one canonical sport.

board_input.description: Unique condition ids independently visible on the provider-first sports board.

board_live_available.description: Whether the always-applicable live-board source completed as available. False can mean a completed source failure (board_source_unavailable) or live-board work missing an internal configured-scope deadline or the outer fair-wave deadline (board_deadline_unavailable); inspect terminals to distinguish them.

board_upcoming_configured.description: Whether a provider-backed upcoming-board source is configured and applicable for this sport. False means not applicable, not provider failure.

board_upcoming_available.description: Whether every configured upcoming-board scope completed as available. False with board_upcoming_configured=false means not applicable. When board_upcoming_configured is true and this flag is false, read board_upcoming_status for the cause (unknown means no cause was recorded, which no computed snapshot reports): the board_source_unavailable and board_deadline_unavailable terminals are assigned only to already-started rows (the live half) and are structurally 0 for the upcoming source, so they never explain this flag.

board_upcoming_status.description: Why the upcoming-board source is (un)available. Board supply is one canonical-sport union: the bare category owns live truth and every configured composed league scope contributes upcoming rows; folded leagues without a configured board (currently CFL) are not in the upcoming union. available: every configured scope completed truthfully (a successful empty schedule still counts). capacity_limited: provider pagination or a configured upcoming cache published an intentionally bounded complete-event prefix; those rows are excluded from diagnostic-universe input and must not be treated as a complete upcoming universe. Cache-bound prefixes are limited to an exact 5,000,000-byte final envelope. source_unavailable: composition failed before a truthful union; resolved scope readers turn half failures into cold_unavailable, so fresh producers are whole-union identity reconciliation or a registry contract failure and carry zero rows. cold_unavailable: every scope completed but at least one reported its upcoming half unavailable because no servable entry was inside the stale-serve bound and the background warm did not land in time; it is not by itself proof of a provider outage. deadline_unavailable: an internal configured-scope deadline or the outer bounded fair wave expired. An internal deadline may retain healthy bare-category or sibling-scope rows; the outer wave records zero rows. These upcoming fields do not describe league live-membership availability. If the bare-category live scope fails, all live rows are dropped even when a league scope completed, because the bare category is the sole live-truth owner. not_configured: no upcoming scope applies to the sport. unknown: no cause was recorded; every computed snapshot reports a concrete status, so none reads unknown. board_upcoming_available is exactly board_upcoming_status == available.

board_upcoming_unavailable_scopes.description: Configured upcoming scopes that did not complete as available. Values are category, a provider league tag slug (nfl, cfb, nba, wnba, euroleague-basketball, ncaa-basketball, cwbb, nhl, mls, valorant, league-of-legends, counter-strike-2, or dota-2), registry when the compiled scope/projection contract drifted, union when cross-scope identity reconciliation failed, or wave when the outer fair-wave deadline expired before scope-level evidence returned. Empty means no unavailable upcoming scope was identified; this includes healthy/not-configured rows and a legacy cached row. Observation league scopes are upcoming-only and perform no live-membership read.

input.description: Stored-universe rows plus provider-board rows missing from storage.

terminals.description: Sparse counts over the closed 25-value terminal vocabulary: outside_horizon, resolved, provider_closed, provider_excluded, invalid_market, missing_token, missing_stored_market, not_provider_live, board_source_unavailable, board_deadline_unavailable, primary_slate_candidate, zero_indexed_holder_research, capacity_limited, provider_unavailable, holder_deadline_unavailable, holder_computation_unavailable, holder_scan_incomplete, no_current_graded_holder, split_holder_pile, price_unavailable, wider_holder_emitted, in_play_emitted, in_play_stale_observed, in_play_directional_unavailable, or internal_unclassified. primary_slate_candidate means the view=signals snapshot named by signals_as_of lists the market at its widest selection (horizon_hours=48, min_grade=B, no selector), so it is not a wider_holder candidate; when no view=signals snapshot could be read (signals_as_of null), no market takes it. capacity_limited is intentional bounded provider-work admission, is fully accounted here, and does not itself set degraded=true. board_source_unavailable means a completed board source was unavailable; board_deadline_unavailable means live-board work missed either an internal configured-scope deadline or the outer fair-wave deadline; provider_unavailable means a holder read sent to the provider failed and the market had no reusable holder page; holder_deadline_unavailable means holder cache/provider work missed the absolute request deadline, or local capacity never sent the holder read, and the market had no reusable holder page; holder_computation_unavailable means post-holder provider or DB-backed price/metadata evaluation was unavailable.

terminal_total.description: Sum of every sparse terminal count.

reconciled.description: True exactly when input equals terminal_total.

EdgeHunterObservationTerminalReason.description: Closed 25-value terminal-reason vocabulary for the accountable Edge Hunter observation funnel. capacity_limited is intentional bounded provider-work admission and does not itself set the snapshot degraded. board_source_unavailable is a completed board-source failure; board_deadline_unavailable means live-board work missed either an internal configured-scope deadline or the outer fair-wave deadline; both classify only already-started rows, so for the upcoming source read funnel.sports[].board_upcoming_status instead; provider_unavailable is reserved for a holder read sent to the provider that failed, with no reusable holder page; holder_deadline_unavailable is holder cache/provider absolute-deadline exhaustion or a holder read local capacity never sent, with no reusable holder page.

selection.description: Normalized axes requested with a selector or category; omitted on an unselected default read.
Normalized axes requested with a selector or category; omitted on an unselected default read.

EdgeHunterSignalsResponse.description: Full Edge Hunter signals list envelope. The view literal distinguishes advanced collections, including empty pages.

EdgeHunterObservationDegradationReason.description: One observed cause of operational degradation in the canonical all-sports observation generation. Reasons are independent of the one-terminal-per-input funnel and remain unchanged through category, cohort and selector projection. Intentional capacity limits and an unconfigured upcoming source are not degradation reasons.

reason.description: Recorded producer cause. holder_scan_incomplete is retired and no longer emitted: the one-page holder read is an intentional bound, disclosed by each row's holder_scan_complete and by coverage.incomplete_holder_markets, and it does not degrade a generation. directional_unavailable can accompany an emitted wider_holder row; live_source_stale means provider live evidence exceeded its freshness bound. Other values identify reconciliation, applicable board-source or terminal failure evidence.

sport.description: Canonical sport for the recorded cause; null only for generation-wide evidence without a sport attribution.

EdgeHunterObservationCoverage.description: Measured coverage of the frozen canonical observation generation and this requested page. For sports and esports reads, the first four counts remain global through category, cohort and all selectors; with admission=most_held_48h they count that selection's generation, where every wider_holder candidate it did not take is capacity_limited. They are neither a census of all provider markets nor a count of successfully evaluated holders. Selected and returned counts describe the requested projection. An unmappable legacy category synthesizes a zero-work empty generation with all six counts zero and no degradation reasons; it does not read the all-sports cache.

input_markets.description: Sum of canonical source-generation funnel input across all sports, before category, cohort or selector projection.

capacity_limited_markets.description: Canonical source-generation input assigned capacity_limited. These markets were intentionally outside the bounded holder-work admission and are not missing emitted rows. It includes the admitted pregame wider_holder markets of any sport no request named in the last 30 minutes, whose holders the generation did not read.

emitted_observations.description: All wider_holder and in_play observations emitted in the canonical source generation, before cohort, category or selector projection. Emerging pile is an overlapping projection and does not add source emissions.

incomplete_holder_markets.description: Canonical source-generation markets whose attempted holder scan did not establish complete coverage, including incomplete scans that did not emit an observation. Collection reads one 100-row page per token, so a market with more holders on a token counts here by design; this count does not by itself degrade the generation.

selected_observations.description: Observations matching the requested cohort, category, selectors and applicable pinned projection cutoff before pagination.

returned_observations.description: Observation rows on this page; equals data.length.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page. Always sent; null on the last page.

snapshot_as_of.description: Completion time of the shared observation snapshot pinned by the cursor.

degraded.description: True when an operational failure or unknown provider-board, holder, directional, reconciliation, or internal completeness state made this snapshot partial. This is snapshot-wide and can retain degradation that the funnel's one-terminal-per-input accounting cannot represent. Inspect degradation_reasons for every recorded source-generation cause and its nullable canonical sport attribution. Intentional bounds do not by themselves set this field: capacity_limited rows remain fully accounted in the funnel, and a holder scan the one-page read leaves incomplete counts in coverage.incomplete_holder_markets; board_upcoming_status=not_configured is not a failure.

degradation_reasons.description: Sorted, deduplicated causes from the canonical all-sports generation, unchanged by category, cohort or selectors; with admission=most_held_48h, from that selection's generation. Empty exactly when degraded is false. Capacity-limited input, the one-page holder bound (holder_scan_complete=false) and board_upcoming_status=not_configured do not by themselves add a reason.

selection.description: Normalized axes requested with a selector or category; omitted on an unselected default read.

admission.description: Echoes the opt-in admission rule a request named; omitted on a default read. When present, data, funnel, coverage, degraded and degradation_reasons describe that selection, not the default one.

departures.description: cohort=wider_holder only, for the default selection and for admission=most_held_48h: markets that had a wider_holder card in an earlier snapshot of the same selection, have none in this one, and have not kicked off. Newest departed_at first. An entry stays until the game_start_time it carries passes, and leaves as soon as the market has a card again; while it stays, its reason changes only while it reports an unfinished read or when view=signals starts or stops listing the market (see reason), and a later departure of the same market is a new entry. Filtered by the same category and selectors as data, and identical on every page of one snapshot. At most 336 entries; when more are open, the oldest departures leave first. An empty array means no card of this selection is departed. Omitted on in_play and emerging_pile, and on a snapshot that could not establish its departures, never reported as an empty array. Tracking that restarts after its record is lost starts empty.

signals_as_of.description: The ranked_at of the view=signals snapshot whose listed markets this snapshot excluded from wider_holder as primary_slate_candidate. The refresh that computed this snapshot read it as it started, so it can be one refresh older than the view=signals snapshot a reader sees at the same moment. null when no view=signals snapshot could be read: that refresh excluded no market, and the funnel counts no primary_slate_candidate. Omitted on an unmappable legacy category, which reads no generation.

EdgeHunterObservationsResponse.description: Full Edge Hunter observations list envelope. Required degradation_reasons explains the source-generation verdict; required coverage distinguishes source input, intentional capacity exclusions, source emissions, incomplete holder scans, selection and the returned page. The view literal distinguishes advanced collections, including empty pages.

EdgeHunterObservationDeparture.description: A market whose wider_holder card left this selection before kickoff, with why it left.

condition_id.description: Raw Polymarket condition id.

category.description: Canonical sport bucket the departed card carried.

admitted_by.description: The departed card's admitted_by: most_held_48h on an admission=most_held_48h response.

game_start_time.description: Kickoff the departed card carried, in UTC. The entry leaves the list once it passes.

last_observed_at.description: The departed card's observed_at: when its last evaluation finished.

departed_at.description: snapshot_as_of of the first snapshot of this selection without the card.

reason.description: Why the market has no card: its terminal in this selection's funnel in the snapshot it left, and while that terminal reports a read that did not finish (holder_deadline_unavailable, provider_unavailable, holder_computation_unavailable, internal_unclassified), the terminal of each later snapshot until one answers; an answered reason stays, except as view=signals starts or stops listing the market. primary_slate_candidate: view=signals lists the market. While the entry stays, a later snapshot that read view=signals and no longer excludes the market replaces it with that snapshot's terminal, one that excludes the market replaces any other reason with it, and one with signals_as_of null leaves it as it is. capacity_limited: it lost its evaluation place without another outcome. missing_stored_market: the market was no longer in the stored market universe. Any other value means what it means in the funnel, for example split_holder_pile, no_current_graded_holder or resolved.

EdgeHunterSelection.description: Normalized requested selection axes. Only requested axes appear; omitted for unselected defaults. Arrays are nonempty, sorted and deduplicated. OR within an axis, AND across axes.

category.description: Resolved legacy canonical bucket or non_sport for an unmappable category.

sports.description: Canonical sport buckets, including Esports and Table Tennis, matched case-insensitively. Unknown names and league aliases such as NFL are rejected in sports; use category for legacy bucket aliases or leagues for exact league selection. Omission covers every sport admitted by the selected view.

leagues.description: Normalized machine/provider league identities, such as nfl, cfb, nba, epl, cs2, lol, dota2 or valorant. Known wire/tag aliases normalize; other provider keys match exact lowercase identity. This is separate from category: category=NFL selects Football, while leagues=nfl selects NFL only. Read market_context.league for authoritative values.

market_types.description: Exact provider sports_market_type values. This is an open provider taxonomy, distinct from exact market IDs. Read market_context.market_type; missing selected metadata excludes the row.

condition_ids.description: Exact market selections. Raw provider condition IDs and the existing mkt_-prefixed aliases normalize to raw IDs. Unknown well-formed IDs return an empty result.

event_slugs.description: Exact provider event slugs. Use event_slug returned on the row; no title or slug-prefix guessing.

series_slugs.description: Exact provider series slugs. Read market_context.series_slug; a missing selected series excludes the row.

EdgeHunterMarketContext.description: Metadata frozen with the read generation. Values are nullable when the provider/canonical source has no value; no title-based inference or current-clock fallback.

league.description: Normalized machine/provider league identity. Known wire/tag aliases normalize; other provider identities match exact lowercase keys.

series_slug.description: Exact provider series slug, usable in series_slugs selection.

market_type.description: Exact provider sports_market_type, usable in market_types selection.

metadata_updated_at.description: Exact local canonical metadata writer market_canonical.updated_at. This is not a provider observation clock; null means unavailable.

SubscriptionRequired.description: Active Pro subscription required. The key is valid but the account has no active Pro subscription; error.reason is subscription_inactive and error.message names the reactivation URL (https://0xinsider.com/billing). Permanent until a person reactivates: no Retry-After, never retry on a schedule.

RequestTimeout.description: Request exceeded the server's 30-second transport timeout. The timeout response has an empty body because it is generated before handler-level JSON error shaping.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. Three independent budgets. (1) 100 requests/minute per user on Pro, 200 on Max (sliding window), on every authenticated route; RateLimit-Limit reports the caller's. On the remote MCP endpoint /api/v1/mcp only tools/call is counted: initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications, and the GET, HEAD and DELETE the endpoint answers 405 spend no per-minute request, no monthly quota and no pay-as-you-go usage, with or without a key. (2) On the BATCH routes only: 2500 batch item units/minute per user on Pro, 5000 on Max, reserved before any item is executed. A batch with N requested items costs N item units, including duplicate and invalid items. 2500 = 100 requests x 25 items per batch on Pro, 5000 = 200 x 25 on Max, which is the most item work a key can buy through the request limiter at all: a caller may spend their plan's entire request minute on full 25-item batches without the item budget being what stops them. The REQUEST budget is the effective ceiling, and batching is never the more expensive choice. The item budget can still deny at a sliding-window boundary (both counters carry the previous window forward with a floor, and the item counter runs 25x the request counter), so honor a 429 from either. Over-quota batches return 429 with Retry-After plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset before any item work is done. (3) The monthly quota: Pro includes 500,000 and Max includes 2,000,000 authenticated requests per UTC calendar month. Over the plan's included requests: with pay as you go on, the excess bills at USD 0.20 per 1,000 on a monthly invoice, up to four times the included allowance (2,000,000 requests for Pro); without it, from October 1, 2026, the next request answers 429 rate_limited with error.reason monthly_quota_exceeded and a Retry-After to the month's reset. Pay-as-you-go accounts receive the same refusal at their ceiling. A refused request is not counted. X-Monthly-Quota-Limit, X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining, and X-Monthly-Quota-Reset (unix seconds, the first of next month) are on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call. (4) The per-address budget: 1200 requests/minute per IP, shared by every caller behind one address and counted before authentication, on every route. A 429 from it carries error.reason ip_rate_limited and describes that bucket in RateLimit-*; a throttled address (sustained over-limit traffic) carries error.reason ip_throttled with a Retry-After of minutes to days, and a request before it does not shorten the cooldown. Every 429 is the standard error envelope with meta.request_id equal to X-Request-Id.

RateLimitUnavailable.description: Redis-backed authenticated rate limiter unavailable; retry after the per-process outage cooldown

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the middleware will probe the Redis-backed rate limiter again.

IdempotencyInProgress.description: An Idempotency-Key request with the same body is still in progress. Retry shortly with the same key and body.

error.message: Your previous request is still processing. Retry in a moment.

IdempotencyConflict.description: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.

different_body.summary: Idempotency key reused with a different body

error.message: Idempotency-Key already used with a different request body

PickNotReleased.description:
No pick is published for the current product day. Scheduled selections retain their returned release time. The product day uses America/New_York, and a day can have no published picks.

The body carries `error.code="not_found"`, `error.reason="pick_not_released"`, and `error.retry_at`. The response sets `Retry-After`. Both retry fields name the same recommended future instant.

The recommendation is advisory and can change. Schedule the next request from the returned retry guidance instead of calculating a release schedule or polling.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the recommended next request. Always at least 1. Names the same instant as `error.retry_at`. Prefer this header for the sleep duration; it is immune to clock skew.

ReadModelWarming.description: Service unavailable. On this route a 503 has TWO distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="read_model_warming": the requested endpoint cannot serve its read model yet. Exact causes are endpoint-specific and can include a cold or contended refresh or a dependency that prevented refresh; consult that endpoint's contract and do not infer dependency health from this shared reason. This is endpoint-local unavailability, not rate limiting: retry only this route after Retry-After (or error.retry_at), and do not feed it into a rate-limit backoff shared with other endpoints. (2) no error.reason: the Redis-backed authenticated rate limiter is unavailable and the middleware failed closed; Retry-After is the seconds until it probes Redis again. Both carry error.code="rate_limit_unavailable" (a FROZEN contract value, so it cannot be split per cause) and X-Request-Id -- which is why error.reason, not error.code, is the discriminator.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until retrying is worth doing. With error.reason="read_model_warming" this is the endpoint-local read-model retry interval; without a reason it is the rate-limiter outage cooldown. Always >= 1.

CursorExpired.description: Bad request. On this cursor-paginated route a 400 has TWO distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="cursor_expired" (with error.param="cursor"): the pagination cursor was invalidated by an upstream data change mid-walk (e.g. the ranking snapshot behind the page refreshed). It is NOT a malformed parameter and NOT a reason to stop: recovery is mechanical -- re-request the first page and walk forward again. There is deliberately no Retry-After and no error.retry_at, because waiting changes nothing. (2) no error.reason: an ordinary invalid request parameter -- check error.param when present, otherwise error.message. Both carry error.code="bad_request" (a FROZEN contract value), so error.reason is the discriminator.

TraderNotTracked.description: Not found. On this route a 404 has THREE distinct causes; branch on error.reason. (1) error.reason="trader_not_tracked": the wallet is real and the URL is right, but the trader is not on the warm sync tier (the wallets we sync most often), so we capture no timeline for them. This is TERMINAL -- there is no Retry-After and no error.retry_at, because neither retrying nor re-spelling the path will ever succeed. Stop requesting this wallet. (2) no error.reason: the trader id or address does not resolve at all. Both carry error.code="not_found" (a FROZEN contract value), so error.reason is the discriminator -- and since this endpoint has singular and plural path spellings, "I used the wrong URL" is a plausible enough wrong guess that the distinction is worth branching on. (3) error.reason="market_out_of_scope" (#27311): condition_id names a market outside sports and esports, which 0xinsider serves exclusively. This is terminal too: stop requesting this market.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594 HTTP-date when this deprecated alias stops serving: 2027-02-01T00:00:00Z (#29351). From that instant the path answers 410 Gone with error.code endpoint_retired; call the successor its Link header names (rel="successor-version").

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Request limit of the budget this request was counted against, for its current window: the API key's per-minute sliding window on an authenticated call, at its plan's limit (100 requests on Pro, 200 on Max); the control-plane bucket GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage share, the same on every plan, on a 429 from either; and the per-IP budget on a public route, on a refused credential (401, 402, 403, 423), and on a remote MCP message other than tools/call.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Request limit of the budget this request was counted against, for its current window: the API key's per-minute sliding window on an authenticated call, at its plan's limit (100 requests on Pro, 200 on Max); the control-plane bucket GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage share, the same on every plan, on a 429 from either; and the per-IP budget on a public route, on a refused credential (401, 402, 403, 423), and on a remote MCP message other than tools/call, none of which reaches the per-key limiter. Standard RateLimit header spelling.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in that budget's current window after this response.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp when that budget's current window resets.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in that budget's current window after this response. Standard RateLimit header spelling.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until that budget's current window resets. Standard RateLimit header spelling.

X-Request-Id.description: Server-generated request identifier for support and tracing. On every /api/v1 response, including 304, 408, CORS preflights and every error, and always equal to meta.request_id in the body. It is the key of the request's usage accounting row and of every log line the request emitted, so quote either form to support. A client-supplied X-Request-Id request header is ignored: the value is never adopted or echoed.

X-Monthly-Quota-Limit.description: Authenticated requests the account's plan includes per UTC calendar month (#16111): 500,000 for Pro, 2,000,000 for Max. Present on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call.

X-Monthly-Quota-Remaining.description: Included requests left this UTC calendar month; 0 once the quota is used. Present on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call.

X-Monthly-Quota-Reset.description: Unix seconds: the first instant of the next UTC calendar month, when the quota resets. Present on every response a route answers for a counted request, on the monthly-quota 429, and on GET /api/v1/me and GET /api/v1/usage, which read the month without spending it. Any other refusal or failure before the route runs, such as a per-minute 429 or a 401, carries none, nor does a remote MCP message other than tools/call.

ETag.description: Weak semantic validator for conditional GET. Request-specific response metadata is excluded; send as If-None-Match to receive 304 when the stable payload is unchanged.

X-Usage-Accounting.description: Usage-record persistence for a protected V1 handler response. persisted: confirmed row; failed: write failed; unknown: completion could not be confirmed. Independent of handler success; do not replay successful mutations to repair accounting. Absent before accounting admission and on public routes. The zero-cost /api/v1/usage route also omits it.

Server-Timing.description: Processing time in milliseconds, for example api;dur=12.345. Includes API authentication, quota admission, handler work and response construction. Excludes network transit and streamed body or export-file transfer. The engineering budget is strictly below 250 ms; this header reports observations, not a latency guarantee or a new timeout.

X-Query-Ignored.description: Comma-separated, percent-encoded query names the operation did not publish and therefore ignored in compatible mode. Names are sorted and de-duplicated.

X-Effective-Query.description: Normalized, percent-encoded query string containing only the recognized names and values applied by the operation. Query names and values use form-urlencoded decoding, where + is a space. Repeated names are retained and sorted by name. A limit outside the operation's published minimum..maximum is reported as the clamped value the page used, so the header states the page size served rather than the one requested.
